The marking itself is one small `reg_mark_ref_group()` called after the spread: `refcol = TRUE` on every `model` / `emp` column whose `col_group` is the first split level. ⚠ **Only after the spread** — `fmt_attr_rules$refcol` merges `"same"` and falls to its neutral on disagreement, so a per-group stamp cannot survive the `vec_rbind()`, and in the stacked shape the reference group is a block of ROWS where a reference COLUMN would be a lie. The synthesised `n` column stays unmarked (it carries no estimate to be a baseline for). Everything downstream already understood `"group"`: the block is now bold in the exports (`rd$bold_cols`), full-strength under greying, and its legend block reads *"Reference group."* on its own.

**The verbose `between_groups` message is deleted** — it priced an internal fit, and the forcing happens in `reg_stage_split()` regardless, so nothing behaves differently.

**The stars sentence is one sentence again** (E2). The regression variant had become *"significantly different from no effect (the reference category in bold; for the Constant, the null value)"*; every table now says *"significantly different from the reference category (in bold)"* — which also collapses two msgids into one — and the Constant is a short aside, **appended only where that row is actually populated**, naming the null `EST_SCALES` declares: *"— from 1 for the Constant —"* on a ratio, *"— from 0 —"* on a difference. A `marginal` / `at_reference` / ordinal table has the row but no intercept to show, so it gets the plain sentence; a mixed table whose model columns disagree about their null gets it too.

**`color = "adjustment"`: the legend and the arithmetic said different things, and that was the real defect.** The legend composed the generic lead *"OR ≥ the observed (crude) effect ×1.1"* — a SIGNED move — while `fmt_adjustment_score()` grades distance from the null. **Reproduced on a real cell**: `relig 5-Buddhist`, crude `0.915` → model `0.735`; the model OR is ÷1.25 the crude one, so the legend claimed red while the cell was blue. Per the maintainer's decision the FRAMING was kept (it is the confounding reading, and what the ×1.1 change-in-estimate break encodes) and the legend fixed to match it, through one new declared fact: `MEASURES$<gap>$lead`, a `closure(subject, ref, dir)` read by `legend_tokens_full()`, absent on every other measure. Both gap measures now read *"OR further from no effect than the observed (crude) effect, by ×1.1; …"* / *"closer to no effect …"*, and `between_groups` gets *"…than the reference group's effect"* for free from `legend_ref_phrase()`.

**A REVERSAL now reads as attenuation, which also closes a hole.** `fmt_gap_parts()`'s `sign` gains one line: it is `-1` whenever the estimate and `obs` sit on opposite sides of the null. With two poles a reversal has to be one of them and it belongs on the attenuated side — whatever the observed effect claimed, the model says it is not that — while its magnitude stays the full move, so a big flip reads as a big move. Measured on the maintainer's table (`married ~ race + rincome + relig + age`): every same-side cell keeps its colour to the digit, and only the three straddling cells move (`relig 4-Jewish` `1.097 → 0.773` goes ×1.42 blue → ÷1.42 red; `race Other` and `relig 6-Muslim` were already red and stay). The hole is `sign == 0`: a perfect mirror (`×2 → ÷2`) fell into the "strengthened" arm and painted **slot 4, the deepest blue**, with a collapsed interval; it is slot 8, the deepest red, now. `fmt_adjustment_score()`, `fmt_gap_raw()`, `fmt_gap_bounds()` and `fmt_gap_p()` are untouched — the magnitude is still `|gap|`, which is exactly what `gap_se` is the SE of, so score and interval stay one decomposition. Per the maintainer's decision the reversal is named NOWHERE: the pair of cells already shows it, their `×` and `÷` facing opposite ways.

**French kept working.** Three msgids moved; the two gap leads use a VERB (`s'éloigne de` / `se rapproche de`) rather than an adjective, because the subject is an acronym (`OR`, `RR`, `diff`) that no adjective can safely agree with. `po/R-tabxplor.pot` was regenerated (it was stale by two phases) and `po/R-fr.po` re-merged; the ~106 untranslated and 9 fuzzy msgids are pre-existing debt for Phase 23f. ⚠ `tools::update_pkg_po()` writes `charset=CHARSET` into the pot and then refuses its own merge — set it back to `UTF-8` and run `msgmerge` / `msgfmt` by hand.

**Also updated**: both regression vignettes' colour paragraph gained the reversal rule (one clause each, EN + FR) — the prose already taught strengthened/attenuated correctly, so only the new case was missing.


##### Phase 22b-v — the numeric predictor

Everything a continuous predictor's row does, end to end. ⚠ After 22b-i, which settles what the `n` column holds.

```r
tab_reg(gss_simple, outcome = "party3", predictors = c("race", "rincome", "relig", "age"),
        family = "multinomial")
tab_reg(gss_simple, outcome = "rincome", predictors = c("race", "marital", "relig", "age"),
        family = "ordinal")
```

- **Multinomial and ordinal print a per-1-unit effect**, which is unreadable next to a factor's contrast (`age` shows `1/1.01***`, and the row carries no unit label at all). Root cause: `need_mult` is gated on `reg_fam_glm()` (`R/reg-resolve.R:460-499`), a closed set that excludes both families, so `multiplier` comes back `NULL` — silently, since the informing message fires only when the user passes a non-default value. `reg_fit_multinom()` / `reg_fit_ordinal()` (`R/tab_reg.R:727`, `:774`) take no `multiplier` argument at all. The k-unit rescale is post-hoc arithmetic on the tidied coefficient (`estimate * k`, `se * |k|`, `R/tab_reg.R:1075-1086`), so it applies to their coefficients unchanged.
- **The unit label is verbose and wraps badly**: `age (per 1 SD (13.5))` repeats the variable name, which the variable column already carries, and word-wraps after `SD` when a longer label elsewhere (`Model fit`) would have left room on one line. Wanted: `per SD/13.5`, with the SD count printed only when it is not 1. Root cause of the wrap: the label goes through `tab_wrap_text()` like every other label (`R/tab-export-prep.R:304-312`); root cause of the text: `reg_multiplier_value()` + `reg_stage_rows()` (`R/tab_reg.R:272-284`, `:2835-2846`).
- **A one-row variable's name is not bold.** It is right that it stays horizontal, but it should match the vertical ones. Root cause: `vert <- ... & run$span > 1L` (`R/tab-render-html.R:352-361`) gives `tx-vname` only to a multi-row block, and bold is a row-level fact (`tx-b`) that a numeric predictor's row does not carry.
- **Move the linearity sparkline into the `n` cell**, which is empty for a numeric predictor by design, and give it a small frame in html (a thinner line than the sparkline itself) so an uninformed reader sees a plot rather than stray pixels. In html, make it just a bit wider (around ×1.5), a bit higher (around ×1.2), with a bigger linewidth. Root cause / material already in place: the glyph run is appended to the LEVEL cell (`R/tab_reg.R:2854-2864`) and html already swaps it for an inline `<svg>` (`tx_spark_svg()`, `R/tab-render-html.R:111-143`). ⚠ The glyphs are dropped entirely from the html level cell today — check what actually reaches each backend before moving it. It must be done at render time anyway, so for the console display **there must be a way (or a hack) to do it without creating a "mixed" column in the pillar abbreviation**.


**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 18 | WARN 1 | SKIP 4 | PASS 7812** — **every one of the 18 is the maintainer's uncommitted palette edit**, not this phase: 16 are the one pending `_snaps/golden.md` CSS diff and 2 are its own contrast assertions (see the last paragraph). `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, three man pages with prose-only edits (`man/tabxplor-options.Rd`'s only `\item` change is the two options the maintainer deleted). ⚠ **The 36 `_golden/*.rds` did not move at all**, and `format()` is **byte-identical over all 945 of their fmt-column renderings** in five modes — which is the phase's own load-bearing claim, since it changes the display engine.

**One architectural change, and it deletes the alternative rather than adding to it.** An `fmt` cell cannot hold text, so a sparkline in the base-count cell looked like four render-layer hooks plus a console placeholder. Instead 22b-ii's rule is generalised in one sentence — **a template's non-whitespace TOP-LEVEL literal is content in its own right, so a spent primary blanks a cell only when the template has nothing else to say** — and the sparkline becomes a literal in the `n` cell's own `display`. Console (pillar), Markdown, kable and HTML then all get it from `format()`, the one source of truth, with **no render-layer hook anywhere**: the `<_range>` pillar tag is untouched (`display_primary()` reads the token, never the literal), the reference bold survives, and `tx_spark_svg()` already scanned every emitted cell. The rule is restricted to bracket-group 0, which is what keeps a void p-value or a void percentage blank: `(Chi2)` and `(n=` sit INSIDE a group. Five lines in `format()` (`fmt_class.R`), of which the two that matter are `ok_c <- !void[[primary]] | lit0` and a `wrote` mask on `out[na_out] <- na` — without the second the feature would have shipped console-only, since md / xl / html / transpose all pass `na = ""`. `bold_split` deliberately records **no** primary range on a literal-carried cell: `paint_split()` and `html_cell_text()` both read `NA` as "one plain piece", which is what keeps the curve out of a grey `tx-sec` aside span.

**Proved safe before anything else changed.** Every template the package can emit — `DISPLAY_PRESETS` plus a scan of `R/` plus the generated `{pvalue} (<label>)` — was enumerated and evaluated: **20 templates, the new arm fires on none**, so the change is unreachable by existing output. That is frozen as a test (`test-display-grammar.R`, source-scanning, so a future template with a bare literal cannot silently change a column), and confirmed empirically by the 945-vector `format()` identity check.

**The sparkline stops being a string glued to a label.** `reg_curves()` now runs on the **group's own** `data` and its curves are stored group-keyed in `meta$assumptions` (a `group` column on each curve tibble, `""` when ungrouped), bound from the parts by `reg_bind_assumptions()`. A new declared entry in `materialize_specs()` (`reg_spark`, right after `base_n`) draws it at display time. That is what makes **D3 nearly free**: a per-group curve used to be impossible because `vec_rbind()`, `tab_spread()`'s pivot and `reg_write_group_gap()`'s `reg_skel_key()` all key on `(var, levels)`, so two groups whose labels differed would double the pivot's rows and break the gap match — out of the label, out of the key. A spread table now shows three different curves side by side in `n_White` / `n_Black` / `n_Other`, and a stacked one reads its group off the row's `tab_var`. `linear_level` is stored beside the curves and is not decorative: `shape = "quadratic"` gives a predictor **two** rows, both with no count, and `skeleton$term` does not exist at display time — the `age²` row correctly keeps its empty cell.

**`multiplier` on every family — a net deletion.** `need_mult` loses its `reg_fam_glm()` gate, and the abort, the informing message and `mult_default` go with it. The rescale is hoisted into one `reg_tidy_rescale()` called from three places, so a multinomial's `term × y.level` tidy and an ordinal's slope-only tidy scale exactly as a glm's, before the Wald assembly. Verified against `MASS::polr`: the cumulative OR is `exp(k·β)` to machine precision and the p-value is unchanged (1.34e-70 on both sides). The marginal paths needed nothing — they already read `multiplier` per predictor and already handle the per-category shape. The latent bug this closes: a mixed glm + multinomial table labelled the shared row `per 1 SD` while the multinomial column's numbers were per raw unit, silently.

**The level IS the unit.** `per SD/13.5` replaces `age (per 1 SD (13.5))` — the `var` column already names the variable, and the nested parentheses were what made the label wrap. The count prints only when it is not 1 (`per 2 SD/27`), an explicit multiplier prints bare (`per 10`), and `multiplier = 1` leaves the plain variable name.

**HTML**: the svg FILLS its cell rather than sitting in it — `dx` 3 → 9, `h` 12 → 22, stroke 1.2 → 2.8 with rounded joins, and an `inset` of half the stroke so the extreme bins are not clipped by the viewBox edge. It carries **no frame of its own**: the cell's own border already draws the rectangle. Two CSS rules beside `.tx-pill` — `.tx-spark{display:block;margin:0 auto}` centres it whatever the column's text-align, and `.tx-sparkcell` (emitted on the containing `<td>` by the renderer) drops the numeric right/top geometry for middle/centre and trims the cell padding to a hairline. A plot wants the whole cell where a number wants the column's own geometry, so the cell is tagged rather than the column. ⚠ **The console is a different problem and is not fixable from R**: it is character-aligned exactly (verified line by line at several widths), but U+2581..U+2588 are East-Asian AMBIGUOUS width, so a terminal that treats those as wide -- or whose font lacks them and falls back to another face -- draws them wider than a digit and the sparkline's row looks shifted. The plain-text ladder that used to be the escape hatch (`spark = "ascii"`, `. , - ~ + = * #`) is **deleted** on the maintainer's call -- eight ASCII ranks do not read as a CURVE, and the shape is the whole point, so a reader who cannot see it is better served by no sparkline. `spark` is a plain logical now, and the option doc names the symptom and the two real cures: a console font that carries U+2581..U+2588, or `FALSE`. **Excel** keeps a real editable count: the glyph cells are exactly the NA cells, so they displace no number and are written individually as text after the numeric column (verified in the file — `C4`/`C5` numeric, `C8` an inline string). **The plot** strips them one step later than before: the glyphs now only exist once the fmt column has been rendered.

**The variable name is bold in its own right** in html. It used to be bold only by accident — through `tr.tx-b` when its block's first row happened to be the reference row — which left a one-row block plain beside a bold neighbour. ⚠ Consequence to review: this also bolds a **merged crosstab's** row-variable names, which are mostly plain today (same heading role, so it reads as the uniformity asked for).

**Accepted, and flagged rather than worked around:** under `n = "no"` there is no `n` column, so there is no sparkline — coherent (the option is an explicit opt-out of that column, and `options(tabxplor.spark = )` still governs the curve itself), but a behaviour loss against today, where the glyphs were unconditional. Two roadmap premises were also wrong and are corrected: html never dropped the glyphs from the level cell (`tx_spark_svg()` runs on the *generic* cell path, so it already covered fmt columns), and `reg_curves()` returns `NULL` with several outcomes, so a multi-outcome table has no sparkline at all.

**Tests**: the three 3+ level parity fixtures now pass `multiplier = 1`, the convention Phase 18z9 already set for the glm families — their claim is against the engine's own per-unit coefficient. One new test locks the opposite: per-SD by default on ordinal and multinomial, `est^k`, `se × |k|`, **p unchanged**, factor levels untouched.

⚠ **Two failures and one repair belong to the maintainer's uncommitted work, not to this phase.** `R/tab-options.R` deleted the `signif_levels` / `signif_labels` rows while `tx_stars_ladder()` still read `tx_option_default()` for both, so **every star in the package had silently disappeared** (measured: the golden markdown lost every `***`, and the baseline suite failed on it before this phase started). The dangling reference is repaired here — the default ladder is stated once, as `?tabxplor-options` already promises — because nothing could be verified without it. Still open, and left alone: `R/tab-css.R`'s print `grey` `#595959` → `#888888` fails its own WCAG assertions (`test-print-palette.R:96-97`: 1.8 against the darkest fill where 3 is required, 3.54 on white where 4.5 is required), and it is the second of the three lines in the pending `_snaps/golden.md` diff — the other two are this phase's `.tx-spark` rules. **`snapshot_accept("golden")` is a one-command step once the palette is settled.**

##### Phase 22b-vi — estimand, fit and the argument surface

- **`reg_spec_build_one()` tests the internal LINK key where it must test the outcome family.** `grouped <- sp_fam == "binomial" && !is.null(sp$trials) && !isTRUE(sp$compound)` (`R/reg-spec-build.R:149`) is exactly what the `⚠` above `reg_is_grouped_binomial()` (`R/tab_reg.R:100-104`) forbids: `rr` and `rd` are binomial fits under another link. Reproduced — `tab_reg(..., trials = k, measure = "ratio")` resolves to `fit = "rr"`, where the inline test answers FALSE and the declared predicate TRUE. The flag feeds `reg_gof_rows()` and `reg_check_rows()`, so a summed score on those two measures gets its Pearson-dispersion footer row and its dispersion check computed as an ungrouped binary logit. Every other caller uses the predicate.
- **The collapsible-link redundancy.** A marginal contrast equals the conditional one exactly when `measure` is the family's own coefficient default (`REG_ESTIMANDS[[fam]]$default[["coefficient"]]`, `R/reg-estimand.R:352-417`) — so `poisson × {marginal, at_reference} × ratio` runs a g-computation sweep and influence functions to return `exp(coef)` under a different name, which the header and legend then present as a distinct estimand. ⚠ A blanket refusal would be wrong twice over: `shape = poly(age, 2)` breaks the identity, and on gaussian the redundant cell IS the family's marginal default, so refusing it would make a bare `effect = "marginal"` an error on a numeric outcome — while the vignette teaches that identity as a pedagogical point. Recommendation: a message, not an abort, suppressed where `shape` makes the identity false. Whatever is decided moves one cell of the combination grid in `?tab_reg` and both regression vignettes.

  | combination                       | vs the coefficient | why                                                   |
  |-----------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
  | poisson × ratio *(its default)*   | **2.2e-16**        | log link: the averaging factorises out of `exp(b)`    |
  | gaussian × difference *(default)* | identical          | identity link                                         |
  | gaussian × ratio                  | 6.0e-03            | different FITS: an lm g-computed vs the log-link `mr` |
  | binomial × ratio                  | 1.8e-02            | logit g-computation vs the modified Poisson           |
  | binomial × difference             | 2.1e+00            | —                                                     |

- **Tidyselect in `tab_reg()`.** The two main user-facing functions must select variables the same way: `tab()` uses `rlang::enquo()` + `tidyselect::eval_select()` (`R/tab.R:286-312`), `tab_reg()` takes plain character (`R/reg-resolve.R:141-153`). ⚠ Both escape hatches must survive: the named list of character vectors (the model comparison) and the two-sided formula.
- **Expose the fitted formulas.** Table metadata plus an accessor, taught in the regression vignette and used by an expert to check what actually reached `glm()`. Root cause of the gap: for the ordinary path the assembled formula is never persisted — `reg_call(x)$fit_spec$specs` carries `outcome` / `predictors`, and `sp$formula` is non-NULL only for the compound escape hatch; the string is rebuilt on demand inside `reg_fit()` (`R/tab_reg.R:1019-1034`).
- **Move `parallel` into `...`** in `tab()` and `tab_reg()`, or drop it in favour of its option twin. It is a declared `TAB_ARGS` entry with an option (`R/tab-args.R:493-517`); both signatures already have a validated `...` (`tab_check_dots()`), so this is a small move that shortens two long signatures.
- ⚠ `multiplier`, `shape` and `ref` keep their shape here: 22b-vii's study settled E6 against a merged spec, and **22b-viii** unifies their grammar instead.

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 18 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 7810** (7816 before; the count moves because two tests became refusals). ⚠ **All 18 failures are PRE-EXISTING at HEAD and none is from this phase** — verified against `git show HEAD`: `R/tab-css.R` already emits the `.tx-spark` / `.tx-sparkcell` rules (22b-v) and the print `grey` `#888888`, while `tests/testthat/_snaps/golden.md` carries neither, so 16 are the one pending golden CSS snapshot and 2 are `test-print-palette.R:96-97`'s WCAG assertions against that grey (1.8 where 3 is required, 3.54 where 4.5 is). Both were already recorded as open at the end of 22b-v; `snapshot_accept("golden")` is still one command once the maintainer settles the contrast. `devtools::document()` clean; **NAMESPACE gains exactly `reg_formulas`**.

**The grouped-binomial predicate, fixed where it was re-derived.** `reg-spec-build.R:164` tested `sp_fam == "binomial"` — the LINK key, which is exactly what the `⚠` above `reg_is_grouped_binomial()` forbids, since `rr` and `rd` are binomial fits under another link. Inert today (`reg_footer_stats()` short-circuits on `REG_FIT_ONLY_FAMILIES`, `reg_glance()` returns early), so a landmine rather than a wrong number: the day those links gain a dispersion row the footer would have been silently wrong. It reads the declared predicate now, and the third argument has one spelling everywhere (`sp$compound`, the spec's own field, replacing `!is.null(sp$formula)` at the two sites that spelled it the other way).

**Two estimands are REFUSED, not noted** (maintainer's decision, this session — Phase 22b-iv's deletion of a purely descriptive note settled that a message which changes nothing does not earn its place). Where the link is collapsible and the marginal contrast runs on the same fit for the same measure, the sweep returns the coefficient under a second header — `gaussian × marginal × difference` bit-identically, `poisson`/`quasipoisson × marginal × ratio` to 2.2e-16 — and one quantity may not have two names. `tab_reg()` now aborts there with the reason and the one right call: *"`effect = "marginal", measure = "difference"` returns the coefficient itself for "tvhours": the identity link is collapsible, so averaging changes nothing. ℹ Use `effect = "coefficient"` (the default)."* So a bare `effect = "marginal"` on a numeric outcome is an error now, which is the teaching moment; gaussian's `default[["marginal"]]` deliberately stays `"difference"` so `measure = "auto"` lands on it rather than silently switching to a ratio of means.

**DERIVED, not declared row by row** — `reg_mark_redundant()` stamps a fourth `status`, `"redundant"`, over `REG_ESTIMANDS` right after the quasipoisson derivation, from facts the file already carries: `effect == "marginal"`, `builder == "ame"`, `!reg_word_noncollapsible(word)` (`REG_WORDS`' declared flag, which is what refuses an odds ratio), and a `coefficient` row of the same family with the same `fit` AND the same `measure`. So a family added later cannot forget the rule, and nothing else needed a line: every listing consumer already filters on `status == "ok"`, so `reg_estimand_offer_lines()`, `reg_measures_rd()`, `reg_words_rd()` and the generated jamovi grid drop the cells for free. Verified the marked set is EXACTLY those three rows over the whole family × effect × measure grid, and pinned as a test. ⚠ **`at_reference` is deliberately NOT refused**: the estimate is the same, but since 22b-iii `reg_fill_base()` takes its levels from the column's own reference-profile sweep, so the `{base}` beside it differs — a different table. `reg_measures()` DROPS a redundant cell rather than showing it as a status (listing it would be the second name the refusal exists to prevent), and says so in one `@details` line.

**`parallel` is gone from both signatures** (maintainer's decision), and the phase's own bullet was wrong about the cheap version: moving it into `...` would have DELETED its `@param` from both man pages, since `tab_args_rd()` emits only for real formals (`R/tab-args.R:920`) — that is why the dotted `OR` / `add_n` / `chi2` are undocumented, which is fine only because they are deprecated — and a hand-written `@param` would then trip R CMD check's "Documented arguments not in \usage". So `options(tabxplor.parallel =)` is the one switch: a machine-level knob, not a per-table statistical choice. It was new in 2.0.0, so nothing is owed a deprecation.

**And that MOVED the nesting rule into the one place that already claimed it.** `tab_pmap()` shipped `tabxplor.parallel = FALSE` into the daemons, so only the SERIAL branch depended on every unit-construction site remembering `parallel = FALSE`. It now sets the option off around **both** branches (`on.exit`), which is what makes the file header's "enforced here and only here" literally true — and deletes the flag from `tab_rowvar_ctxs()`, from the multi-outcome recursion, and from `reg_stage_split()`'s per-group `reg_build()`. `tab_parallel_workers()` lost its first argument; the ctx field, the `tab_build()` formal and the `TAB_ARGS` row went with it. The one caller that must still force it is the jamovi regression bridge, whose STAGED mode passes no cache env: it sets the option off for the length of the build, where it used to pass `parallel = FALSE`.

**`reg_formulas()` — one assembly, three fitters, and an accessor that cannot drift.** `reg_fit()` built the glm formula inline while the 3+ level engines used `reg_fit_formula()`; the builder is now one function taking the three pieces the glm path needs (`response`, `cross`, `offset`), called twice by `reg_fit()` (the fit and the identity-link fallback) and once by each 3+ level engine. The exported accessor then reads `reg_call(x)$fit_spec$specs` — already persisted, the same recipe `reg_check_plots()` refits from — and calls that same builder, so it reports what really ran without plumbing a formula through the parallel seam. One row per model: `model` / `outcome` / `family` / `fit` (the internal link key) / `formula`. Verified on a plain call, a comparison, two outcomes, `shape = "quadratic"` (the frozen centre shows), a grouped binomial under both links (`cbind(.gb_succ, .gb_fail) ~ race` and `.gb_succ ~ race + offset(log(.gb_trials))`), a compound formula and an ordinal fit; a crosstab is refused. `@details` names the two things the list does not repeat — under `tab_vars` the same formula is fitted within each group, and `color = "between_groups"` fits one extra pooled model for the footer test only.

**One tidy-select grammar, for BOTH producers** (maintainer's decision: a bare symbol holding a character vector must keep working, with no warning). Measured first, which is what kept the helper to one branch: only a **bare symbol** trips tidyselect's "Using an external vector in selections was deprecated" — inline strings, calls, `all_of()` and `do.call`-injected values are all silent — and with a column `a` and an env object `a`, `eval_select` already picks the **column**. So `quo_peek_extern()` fires only when a symbol names no column (tidyselect's own rule, so no selection outcome changes) and `tidy_select_chr()` re-emits the value as `all_of()`, which tidyselect still validates and orders. `tab()`'s five inline `eval_select` sites call it now, so a programmatic `tab(d, rv, marital)` stops warning too; `allow_rename = FALSE` turns the silent rename trap (`c(m = "race")` used to return `"m"`, a column that does not exist) into a clean error, and `DESCRIPTION` moves to `tidyselect (>= 1.2.0)`.

**`tab_reg()` resolves its four roles at a new stage S0**, run by `tab_reg()` itself rather than inside `reg_resolve_args()` — after `tab_check_dots()`, so a mistyped argument still says "unknown argument" instead of dying in tidyselect, and before the multi-outcome recursion, which reads values. Two things are load-bearing and are stated in both headers: it selects against **`svy_select_frame()`** — a new side-effect-free reader of a design's `$variables`, sharing the replicate/two-phase refusal with `svy_unwrap_data()`, which must stay the single unwrap because it informs, adds the reserved columns and computes degf — and an empty selection becomes **`NULL`, not `character(0)`**, since 17 guards downstream test `is.null()`. The two escape hatches are detected on the expression where they are written inline and on the peeked value where they arrive in a variable; a CALL that BUILDS one (`f[[2]]`, `as.formula(s)`) cannot be told from `starts_with()` by its expression, so it is recognised only once selection has FAILED, with any other failure re-raising tidyselect's own message. A `predictors` `list()` now selects **each element on its own**, names preserved — `list(m1 = c(race, age), m2 = starts_with("inc"))` — and the three spellings of a comparison (inline bare, inline character, a variable) were verified to give `identical()` tables. `reg_prepare_data()` keeps every check: the two that tidyselect now guarantees are retagged as invariants for a direct caller, and its three load-bearing ones (tab_vars is not also an outcome or predictor, is a factor / character, and gives every group a fittable level set) are untouched, since tidyselect sees none of them. The jamovi bridge went to `rlang::inject()` + `!!` on the four roles — the warning-free injected-value path `jmvtab-cache.R` already used for `tab()`, and it removes any dependence on no dataset having a column named `dep` or `preds`.

**Three tests moved, for a reason each.** The gaussian-AME parity test now asserts the refusal and its parity claim survives on the `effect = "coefficient"` column, which is the same number — with the p-value compared against `summary(lm)` rather than `marginaleffects`, because a coefficient's p refers to `t(df.residual)` and a marginal effect's to z, so the two differ in the third digit (0.0095017 vs 0.0094894) and only the fit's own value is the contract. `tab_vars = "nope"` now gets tidyselect's *"Column `nope` doesn't exist"* in place of the boundary's *"not a column"*. And the parity file drives both branches through one `with_par()` helper instead of an argument.

**Documentation.** `?tab_reg`'s four role `@param`s carry the tidy-select marker and state the precedence rule (a bare name is a column first; a name that is no column is looked up as an object); `@param effect` no longer says "the coefficient itself for gaussian" but names the refusal. Both regression vignettes' combination grids mark the two cells `≡` with a legend line and a fourth state in the states list, and the `≡` reason is folded into the "when do the three differ?" paragraph. `jamovi/js/jmvtabreg.js`'s generated `TABX_ESTIMANDS` block was regenerated by `dev/generate_jamovi_js.R` (the suite asserts it), so the UI grid drops the two cells too.

**Three stale vignette statements found and fixed on the way**, all contradicting the running package since 22a-iii and sitting in the paragraphs being edited: two said a Poisson `effect = "marginal"` has no observed counterpart (22a-iii gave `REG_EMPIRICAL$poisson` the `diff` shape, so the pair reads `Obs_diff | Model_mdiff` and IS tested), and one still named the retired acronym "MER". Both language versions.

**Reported, not fixed.** In jamovi, `TABX_DEFAULT_MEASURE` still names `difference` as gaussian's marginal default, which is now a refused cell — so a user picking `effect = marginal` there with the default measure gets the abort text in the results panel rather than a greyed control. Correct, but **22g** could grey the contrast instead. And the leaves `tab_plain()` / `tab_num()` still call `eval_select()` directly (they need POSITIONS), so an external character vector still warns there; they are superseded producers, so it was left alone.


##### Phase 22b-vii — research and design: the per-predictor surface, the reference profile, interactions

Per decisions E5 and E6, redirected mid-phase by the maintainer to **research and design only**: no implementation, a detailed study written to `dev/`. Its three parts constrain each other — Part C's interaction needs Part B's declarable reference, and Part B's `ref` is one of Part A's three arguments — so they are designed together and implemented together.

**DONE.** Wrote `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md` (907 lines): decision register, the three parts, a criteria matrix, ten measured captures and the references. **No package file was changed**, so no test run and no `devtools::document()`.

**Five decisions taken with the maintainer, and the study's own verdict.** F1 keep `multiplier` / `shape` / `ref` as three arguments and unify their grammar (no `pred()` constructor: a constructor buys a second mini-language, a jamovi redesign and `ref` diverging from `tab()`, in exchange for name checking that already exists) · F2 `ref` extends to continuous predictors, default the mean · F3 the Constant row is anchored at that declared reference · F4 under `effect = "marginal"` it is the population-average prediction instead · F5 interactions get `cross =`.

**The missing key, and it is the maintainer's own suggestion.** *An interaction is a predictor whose levels are combinations, and whose univariable model is its own saturated fit.* Materialising the pair as a real column before the fit is not a workaround — it is what makes every subsystem work with **no integration at all**: the 2-tier row model already holds it, the cell counts come from `reg_level_counts()`, the crude companion is the existing saturated closed form, the adjustment gap keeps its influence-function interval, the colour ladders / stars / legend / header word are untouched, `svyglm` / `multinom` / `polr` need nothing, and the jamovi key fingerprints the prepared frame so the new column moves it by construction. **Measured, not asserted**: a combined factor renders a complete crude-plus-adjusted table today, with per-cell `n`, observed and adjusted rates, colours and `gap_se` populated on 18 of 21 rows — captured verbatim in the study's §7.4. It is also, independently, the presentation Knol & VanderWeele (2012) recommend: one row per `(G, E)` stratum against a single common reference, with the actual risks in the cells, on both scales.

**The three measurements that decide the design.** (1) `y ~ X*M`, `y ~ M/X` and `y ~ combined_factor` are **the same fit** — identical logLik and rank, fitted values within 5.6e-16 — so the choice among them is a choice of what a ROW SAYS, never a statistical one. (2) R's nesting operator gives the simple slopes **directly as coefficients**, matching `L'β` on the star fit to 1.39e-17 (estimates) and 8.67e-19 (SEs), so the continuous arm needs no contrast engine. (3) The univariable fit of a combined factor **is** the observed cell table: agreement with the two-way closed form 1.4e-12 on estimates, 9.3e-8 on SEs — the crude column is exact by construction, where the classical closed form for a *continuous* crossed predictor drifts with skew (ratio 1.003 at skew 0.24, 1.034 at 0.49) and so stays disqualified.

**Part B, and the maintainer's two questions that REVERSED its route.** The study first proposed anchoring the Constant row by PREDICTING at the reference profile — the prediction on the link scale is the centred intercept exactly, estimate and SE alike (0.2369388 / 0.02878313 both ways), against a raw intercept 2.88× away on the odds scale. The maintainer then asked what that does in a model with an INTERACTION, and whether Part C's "prepare the variable, then let the fit do its job" should not apply to the anchor too. Both points hold, and the second explains the first.

**Measured: a prediction fixes the row it is computed for, and nothing else.** With `married ~ race * age + relig` the Constant identity survives (2.8e-17) but every LOWER-ORDER term is still an effect at age = 0: the `race` rows move from OR 0.334 / 0.424 to 0.402 / **1.163** between the two anchorings — the second by **×2.74**, reversing its reading from "a strong negative effect" to "essentially nothing". A table whose Constant row sits at the mean while its `race` rows sit at zero is internally INCONSISTENT, which is worse than uniformly wrong. So **F3's route is now R2: shift the column at the preparation boundary, beside `reg_shape_apply()`**, and the fit's own coefficients are already anchored — the `L'β` Constant machinery the first draft proposed is deleted before it is written.

**Four of the five arguments the first draft made for predicting are wrong**, and the study says so with the measurements, because a future reader will re-invent them. There is no extra fit (the model is fitted once, on the prepared data). "No intercept to centre" is answered per family, not by prediction. "It leaves the crude column's unit system alone" is FALSE — the crude companion runs through the same `reg_fit()` on the same prepared frame, and a slope is invariant anyway (2.4e-17). The `shape = "quadratic"` collision is an ORDERING rule, not a conflict: shape recodes first (it defines the model's variable), the anchor applies to the result. Only the polynomial-contrast argument stands, and it is off-target — it is about which FACTOR level the profile sits at. Meanwhile centring buys what prediction never could: **it repairs the collinearity check** (max VIF 11.74 raw against 1.28 anchored), the same false alarm the roadmap already recorded for `shape = "quadratic"`.

**Everything that is an estimate is invariant** — fitted values 5.6e-16, logLik 0, the slope 2.4e-17, the interaction coefficients 9.5e-18, the LR test bit-identical, the AME 0 / 2.8e-17, the crude univariable slope 2.4e-17, adjusted predictions 3.3e-16, and `multiplier = "sd"` by construction. So the rule is one sentence: **an estimate never needs un-centring; only a descriptive reading of the variable's own values does** — and there are exactly TWO such readers in the package, `reg_spec_tips_num()`'s tooltip and `reg_panel_linearity()`'s x axis. The sparkline is unaffected (a constant shift does not change a curve's shape).

**And a re-anchor is an exact linear reparametrisation of the fitted object** (`T·b` 1.0e-14, `T·V·T'` 2.2e-16) — the same fact `reg_reref_fit_res()` already exploits for a factor reference change, so the jamovi live path can treat a numeric `ref` change as a cache HIT. It stays an OPTIMISATION rather than the semantics for one measured reason: a profile-likelihood interval is not a linear map, and `method = "profile"` is supported. The refit is exact for `glm` / `svyglm` (6.9e-18) and drifts at 4.6e-07 (`multinom`) / 6.9e-07 (`polr`) — invisible in print, but it is why those goldens may move in their last digits.

The population-average arm must be computed as the model's average prediction, not short-cut to the observed rate: they coincide exactly for a canonical link (0.4872685, weighted 0.4889446) but not for a log-link binomial (0.4859015 vs 0.4872685).

**Three defects found and reported, not fixed.** (1) **A variable whose name needs backticks silently loses its `Overall association (LR)` footer row** — `reg_global_rows()` filters `have %in% sp$predictors` (`R/tab_reg.R:2207`) where `have` is `terms(fit)$term.labels`, which is backticked for a non-syntactic name; measured, `race_age` gets the row and the identical model named `race x age` gets none. Pre-existing and general (any name with a space), and it matters because `race × age` is the natural name for a compound predictor. (2) `reg_reference_grid_values()` uses an unweighted `mean()` while `multiplier` and `shape` measure their centre with `reg_weighted_mean()` on the frozen frame. (3) `reg_tidy_rescale()` matches `td$term == v` exactly, so `multiplier` cannot reach a nested slope term — silent, and only if the nested arm lands. Also confirmed: the collinearity check reads max VIF 11.74 on an interacted fit against 1.28 centred and **1.02** under the compound-predictor parametrisation, which avoids the false alarm entirely.

⚠ **The compound-formula hatch stays.** The roadmap wanted it removed before release; the study recommends keeping it as the expert exit door for a specification the argument surface cannot express (custom contrasts, hand-written offsets, three-way terms), exactly as `empirical = "column"` is. What it must stop being is the *answer to interactions* — its own capture (§7.3) shows why: raw coefficient names, no counts, no crude column, no unit, and the lower-order block reporting its effect at age = 0.

##### Phase 22b-viii — the per-predictor grammar and the reference anchor

Parts A and B of the study, implemented together. **Read `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md` before planning** — most of the design is settled there.

One shared per-predictor resolver and the uniform grammar on `multiplier` / `shape` / `ref` (scalar = every eligible predictor, named = per variable, a reserved `default` name for the rest); `ref` extended to continuous predictors with the mean as its default; **the anchor realised as a column SHIFT at the preparation boundary, beside `reg_shape_apply()` and after it** (shape recodes first — a quantile shape becomes a factor and is never shifted); the Constant row then read from the fit's own intercept, with the population-average arm under `marginal`; the offset added back in the study's two descriptive readers; the row label; defects A2-1 and A2-2. Goldens and the `golden` snapshot move — including the last digits of `multinom` / `polr` cases — so review each diff deliberately. `?tab_reg`'s Constant paragraph currently teaches the opposite and must be rewritten; both regression vignettes gain a paragraph, because with interactions the anchor stops being a detail. The reparametrisation identity (study §3.6) is an optional follow-up for the jamovi fast path, not part of the semantics.

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 20 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 7874** (7820 before; +54 from the tests added here). ⚠ **All 20 failures are the maintainer's in-flight black-and-white chrome / typography palette edit** — 16 are the one pending `_snaps/golden.md` CSS snapshot and 4 are `test-print-palette.R`'s own contrast assertions (`:71`, `:103`, `:104`, `:146`) — and **none is from this phase**. `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, only `man/tab_reg.Rd` and `man/reg_formulas.Rd` rewritten, both with byte-identical `\usage` and identical `\item{}` name sets.

⚠ **Two roadmap/study premises were wrong and are corrected here: NO golden and NO snapshot moves.** No `_golden/*.rds` case and no `_snaps` file builds a `tab_reg()` table (`grep -c tab_reg tests/testthat/helper-golden.R` → 0), so the regression side is golden-blind. What moved is the parity tests that include the intercept, and nothing else. `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md` §3.11 says otherwise and should be read with this correction.

**Part A — one grammar, three arguments, one resolver.** `reg_per_predictor()` (`R/reg-resolve.R`, beside its outcome-axis sibling `reg_per_outcome()`) is now the only parser of a per-predictor argument: an **unnamed** element — or one named `default` — is a **fallback**, a **named** one overrides that variable, and every refusal names the eligible set. Three grammars became one, and three gaps closed with them: `shape = "quintiles"` (the package's own recommended cure for non-linearity) was **inexpressible**, `multiplier` silently discarded the user's scalar the moment any name appeared (so `c("2sd", age = 10)` reverted everything else to `"sd"`), and `ref` warned-and-ignored what the other two aborted on. `reg_resolve_shape()`'s named-vector refusal, `reg_resolve_multiplier()`'s `else default` discard, and `reg_apply_references()` as a validator are **deleted**; `reg_relevel_data()` is the pure rewriter left behind, and `reg_relevel_design()` went with it (its one job was the `design_obj$variables <- data` write-back every other data rewrite of S2 already does at the call site). Two carve-outs stay at the call sites, because they buy a better message than a generic one: `shape`/`multiplier` naming a factor (`reg_check_continuous_names()`), and `ref` naming an outcome ("did you mean `outcome_level`").

**The maintainer's grammar decision, and why it needs no second reserved word.** The two `ref` vocabularies are **disjoint**, so a fallback names its own kind: a number or `"mean"` / `"median"` / `"min"` / `"max"` addresses the continuous predictors, `"first"` / `"last"` the factors. `ref = c("median", "last", race = "Black")` therefore sets **both** defaults in one vector, and `default =` spelled out does the same (twice, if both are wanted — duplicate names are legal in R). A NAMED entry is unambiguous from the other side: there the **variable's** kind picks the vocabulary, so a factor owning a level called `"min"` keeps its own reading. `tab_vars` and the multinomial pivot are addressable **by name only** and never inherit a fallback — the one asymmetry the shared resolver carries, and the reason it takes an `also` slot.

**Part B — the anchor, and where it had to live.** `ref` now names a continuous predictor's anchor, realised by SHIFTING the column so the fit's own coefficients are already anchored (study §3.4's R2). It sits in **S5, not S2** as the study proposed, for a reason the study could not see: `ref`'s eligible set includes the multinomial pivot, which only exists after S3, so anchoring in S2 would force `ref` to be parsed twice — the exact duplication Part A deletes. The boundary's rule is now stated as *S2 defines the model's **variables** (labels → merge → `shape`); S5 fixes their **origin***. S5's blocks were reordered to U0 (`ref` parsed once) → X (the frozen frame) → Y (the shift) → the multiplier's SD and the quadratic terms, on the shifted frame → U (the factor relevel, **last**, because it is the one step the reref path defers). Moving the frozen frame above the relevel is provably a no-op — a relevel changes neither the row set nor any numeric column — and it is what lets the anchor, the SD and the curvature centre come from ONE measurement, which is what that frame already existed to guarantee.

**Measured, on the study's own case.** `married ~ race * age + relig`: max VIF **11.74 → 1.28**, exactly §3.4's figure, and the `race Other` row moves from a strong effect to `1/1.10` — the ×2.74 reversal §3.3 is about. Slopes, intervals, p-values, the LR test and the AME are identical to 1e-9 across `ref = 0` / `"mean"` / `"median"` / a number; only the intercept moves. `ref = c(v = 0)` is bit-identical to the old behaviour, which is what makes it the one-token fix for a parity test.

**One deliberate deviation from the approved plan, and it is what makes the phase's own motivating measurement true.** The plan exempted every **compound formula** from anchoring, on the ground that shifting a column changes what a user's `poly()` / `I()` / `log()` computes. True of a wrapped variable — false of a bare one, and `y ~ race * age` is precisely the bare case the whole of Part B exists for. `reg_formula_bare_vars()` walks the RHS and anchors only a variable the formula uses **as itself** (never one inside a call, `offset()` included), so the interaction case is anchored today rather than waiting for 22b-ix, and `tvhours ~ race + poly(age, 2)` stays parity-identical to `lm()` at **0**.

**`reg_shape_term()` stopped measuring its own centre.** After the shift the anchor *is* where the variable is centred, so the quadratic emits `I((`v`/s)^2)` and takes its square around the DECLARED anchor. Keeping a self-measured `m` would have put the curve at the mean while the linear row sat at the anchor — two answers to one question — and, under the default anchor, frozen a `1.2e-17` literal into the formula string, the skeleton `term` and `reg_formulas()`' output. Under the default anchor the term is IEEE-identical to today's. `reg_check_linearity_rows()` now passes the call's weights while we are there (an inconsistency, **not** a wrong number: the linearity refit contains the linear term, so `span{1, x, (x−m)²/s²} = span{1, x, x²}` and its LR p is invariant to both `m` and `s`).

**The Constant row, all three contrasts.** It is a **baseline**, computed at the very point that column's effects are computed at: the fit's own intercept under `coefficient` (free — after the shift it already is the anchored one), the predicted outcome at the reference profile under `at_reference`, the population average under `marginal`. One new producer, `reg_gcomp_baseline()` (`R/reg-influence.R`), answers all three — `newdata = NULL` averages over the fitted sample with its weights, a one-row frame evaluates at that profile — and `reg_prob_engine()` covers multinomial and ordinal, so **`polr` gets a populated row under `marginal` where it never had one**. `reg_profile_row()` builds that one-row frame from `data` itself, so every factor keeps its full level set (a grid assembled from scratch would drop levels and shorten the model matrix). **Verified: the anchored intercept IS the at-reference prediction** — odds 1.02 ⇒ risk 50.5 %, the study's §3.2 identity, now a test.

**One writer converts it to the column's own geometry**, read off `EST_SCALES` rather than branched per family: an `est_field == "or"` column shows the baseline **odds** (interval on the log-odds), a `mult` column the baseline **risk / rate** (on the log), an additive one the **probability / mean** as it is. A summed score rides the arm's existing `× trials`, so its baseline is a mean SCORE. `reg_marginal_column()` also stopped spelling its scale three times — `"mean_ratio"` / `"odds_ratio"` / `"raw_diff"` were hard-coded in three arms while the estimand's own key was already being passed in; one `sc` resolved at the top now serves every arm.

**No star on a predicted baseline** (maintainer's decision). It carries its interval and no p-value: a predicted 48.7 % is trivially "different from 0", and a star that meant something else there than everywhere else in the table would cost more than it says. `tab_constant_null()` (`R/fmt_class.R`) therefore keys on a finite **p-value** rather than a finite estimate, so the stars legend's "— from 1 for the Constant —" aside appears only on the tables that really test it. Asserted both ways.

**The label is a display fact now.** `"Reference population"` was a bare, untranslated literal duplicated in the two skeleton builders; both collapse into `reg_constant_row()` with the internal key `level = "Constant"`, and `reg_stage_rows()` writes the displayed label beside the multiplier's own `per SD/13.5` — `gettext("Population average")` when **every** outcome resolves to `marginal`, `gettext("Reference profile")` otherwise. A row label cannot be per column, so a table mixing contrasts takes the profile reading, which is the one true of the anchored intercept its other columns show. Both strings are new msgids and are translated (`Moyenne de la population` / `Profil de référence`); the remaining 13 untranslated + 9 fuzzy are pre-existing debt for Phase 23f. The `var` key `"Constant"` never changes — `forest_plot(intercept =)`, `tab_constant_null()` and `reg_level_counts()` all read it.

**The two descriptive readers, and one pre-existing bug fixed with them.** An estimate is invariant under the shift; a description of the variable's own VALUES is not, and there are exactly two: `reg_spec_tips_num()`'s tooltip and `reg_panel_linearity()`'s x axis. Both add the offset back (`reg_anchor_of()` — ⚠ `anchors[[v]]` cannot be used, an absent name is an ERROR on a named numeric, not NULL). ⚠ **`reg_check_plots()` refits from the user's RAW data, and was already silently wrong for every value-recoding `shape`** — `fit_spec` carried `shape_terms` but not the recodes, and the `nobs` guard structurally cannot catch it (the row count is identical). Dropping the quadratic's frozen centre would have made it a three-way hole, so the preparation is stored once (`fit_spec$prep`: the shapes with their quantile BREAKS frozen, plus the anchors) and replayed once (`reg_prepare_replay()`). `reg_curves()` / the sparkline need nothing — a location shift does not change a curve's shape.

**Four defects found and fixed on the way.** (1) **A numeric `ref` change was a jamovi cache HIT returning a WRONG number** — caught by the test written to assert the opposite. `jmv_col_fp()` fingerprints a column's class, levels and NA count, never its values, so a shift is invisible to it; and unlike a factor reference, an anchor is not a reparametrization `reg_reref_fit_res()` can apply. `anchors` is declared in both fit-key `extra` lists now, exactly as `multiplier` is. (2) **`ref = "last"` landed on the wrong level** whenever the last declared level was empty: `reg_fit()` drops empty levels, so the relevel moved a level that then vanished and the reference silently became the next one — `reg_ref_level()` reads `fct_drop()`ed levels now, i.e. the ones the model will see. (3) **A mistyped `multiplier` was silent**: `multiplier = c(age = "banana")` parsed to `NA`, was dropped by the finite filter, and the row printed a per-1-unit effect with no message; `reg_multiplier_ok()` refuses it by name. (4) **A2-1** — `reg_reference_grid_values()`'s unweighted `mean()` is gone: after the shift a numeric's grid value is `0` by construction, so the profile and the unit can no longer disagree, and its fallback (compound formulas only) is the weighted mean. Its character arm also stopped ignoring `ref` (`sort(unique(x))[1]` → the factor's own first level).

**A bare number on a transformed column is refused, not silently subtracted.** `shape = c(age = "log"), ref = c(age = 30)` would take 30 off `log(age)`; it now aborts naming the cure (`ref = c(age = log(30))`), while the four keywords are measured on the transformed column and are always right.

**Tests.** One new file, `tests/testthat/test-reg-anchor.R` (10 tests): the grammar and every refusal, the reparametrization invariance, the weighted-mean default (A2-1), the shape-then-anchor ordering, the three Constant arms with the §3.2 identity, the geometry per scale, the label, and the `reg_check_plots()` replay. Plus the jamovi MISS/HIT pair in `test-jmvtabreg-cache.R`. Existing parity tests took **one token** — `ref = c(<num> = 0)` beside the established `multiplier = 1` idiom — which keeps each assertion exactly what it was and doubles as the "an anchor of 0 is the identity" regression: `test-tab_reg.R` (gaussian, poisson, multinomial, ordinal, the multinomial AME) and `test-tab_reg-survey.R` (six sites). The two `at_reference` tests pin their comparator datagrid at the same declared anchor. `test-reg-shape.R`'s "there is no apply-to-everything form" assertion is **reversed** — that form is the point now.

**Reported, not fixed** (out of scope): jamovi's `ref_levels` control is labelled "Reference levels (per variable)" and now also sets continuous anchors, so its label and help text should be reworded in **22g**'s single `jmvtools::prepare()`; nothing is inert meanwhile, since the folder already emits the named character vector the new grammar accepts (`c(age = "40")` parses as a number by design).


##### Phase 22b-ix — interactions

Part C of the study. **Read `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md`**; it holds the argument surface, the two arms, the criteria matrix and the caveats.

`cross` and its boundary stage (beside `reg_shape_apply()`, which already rewrites columns at the same point and must also write into `design_obj$variables`); the compound column, its level order and its labels; the categorical arm (a combined factor) first, the nested-slope arm second; the reference cell composed from the parents' own `ref`; the interaction test row as one extra additive fit joining `TEST_ROWS`; defects C4-1 and C4-2; the jamovi option; documentation in two languages. The list of what is missing is short by construction — §4.11 — because the design was chosen to make it short.

**Open question to study:**
- Since adding an interaction materialises a compound predictor column, **would it be reliable to pass it in the `predictors =` argument directly with the `"var1:var2"` syntax ?** Would it be user-friendly ? Would it we workable from the tidyselect syntax or asks to remove it ? For example: `predictors = c("race", "rincome", "relig", "tvhours", "race:tvhours")`. Main interests: no new argument ; possibility to skip the main term to only add the interaction (removing `"tvhours"` in the former vector). Would it work ? Can you sea caveats ?

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 7995** (7932 before; +63, from the 13 tests added here). `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, only `man/tab_reg.Rd` and `man/reg_formulas.Rd` rewritten, both with byte-identical `\usage` and identical `\item{}` name sets. ⚠ **Not one `_golden/*.rds` or `_snaps` file moved**, as predicted: no golden case builds a `tab_reg()` table, so the regression side is golden-blind.

**THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND IT DELETED THE ARGUMENT.** `a:b` inside `predictors` works, bare or quoted, and it is strictly better than the study's `cross =`: it needs no new argument (and `cross` was **already taken** internally, by `reg_fit_formula(cross =)`, the pooled `tab_vars` fit), it is **per model** by construction — so `list(additive = c(race, party3), crossed = c(race:party3))` is an ordinary model comparison, the thing the roadmap had deferred as "per-model `shape`" — and the parents need no magic removal, because the user simply does not list them. The one cost, measured and accepted: **a bare `a:b` no longer selects a column RANGE inside `predictors`**. That is not a loss but a repair — before this phase `predictors = c(race, age4, race:age4)` selected the columns *between* `race` and `age4` and fitted a silently wrong model with no error at all. `all_of()` still gives a range; nothing released depended on it.

**One rule, and the phase is a preparation step rather than a feature.** *An interaction is a predictor whose levels are combinations, and whose univariable model is its own saturated fit.* Prepare the pair as a variable and there is nothing to integrate — `reg_skeleton()`'s `term = paste0(var, level)`, `reg_column()`'s join on that term, `reg_level_counts()`, `reg_crude_saturated()`, `reg_reference_grid_values()` and `reg_marginal_gcomp()`'s level sweep all read a factor COLUMN generically. The new file `R/reg-cross.R` is 300 lines and the rest of the package barely moved.

**Two arms, declared in `REG_CROSS_ARMS`, chosen by what the MODIFIED parent is.** `race:party3` (both categorical) materialises **one combined factor**, every observed cell against one common reference cell — the presentation Knol & VanderWeele (2012) recommend, with the actual rates in the cells. `age:race` (a continuous modified predictor) emits the **nested term** `M:X` beside the moderator's own main effect, i.e. R's `M/X`, whose rows are the slope within each level. Both parents are supplied BY the cross and listing one beside it aborts — rank-deficient in the first arm, a silent reparametrisation in the second (R gives full dummy coding, one slope per level, precisely because the modified variable has no main effect). ⚠ **the parent rule is PER MODEL, never across the list**, or the with/without comparison it exists for would be refused.

**The measurements that carry the design, all reproduced here.** The three parametrisations are ONE fit — `y ~ race*age4` and the combined factor agree on logLik and rank with fitted values within **3.3e-15**, so the choice is of presentation and never of statistics. The crude column of a combined factor **is** the observed cell table, exact to **1e-9** against the two-way tabulation, because a factor already takes the saturated closed form. A nested block's slopes are `glm(y ~ M/X)`'s own coefficients (**1e-9**, per SD), and its crude twin is that model's univariable fit (**exact**). And a crossed slope's subgroup AME equals `marginaleffects::avg_comparisons(variables = list(age = k), by = "race")` to **1e-8**.

**Full `effect` support cost three lines, because of one thing the engine already was.** Every quantity `reg_gcomp_maker()` produces — `est`, `emp`, `G`, `mean1`, `mean0` — is a WEIGHTED MEAN, so **a subgroup effect is the same sweep under a restricted weight vector**. The closure gained a `mask` argument, `w <- w0 * mask` and `sw <- sum(w)`; `reg_gcomp_cat_maker()` took the same three lines, `reg_ame_if_maker()` / `reg_ame_if_cat_maker()` pass it through, and the **gap SE therefore came for free**. `reg_marginal_me()` covers the `at = "reference"` half with `by =` and a per-level datagrid. `marginal` and `at_reference` work on both arms, and each nested row carries its group's own adjusted prediction — the level a bare slope never had.

**`sp$row_vars`: a spec now says what it FITS and what it SHOWS, separately.** A nested block's name is not a formula term, so five sites keyed on `sp$predictors` were reading the wrong list: `reg_cols_coef()`'s `model_predictors`, `reg_gap_se_columns()`'s `in_mod`, `reg_marginal_column()` (×3), `reg_fill_base()` and every `reg_fill_sweep()`. They read the declared row blocks now, and `sp$cross` carries the model's keys so **every rebuild of the formula reads one fact** — `reg_fit()`, `reg_formulas()`, the crude fit and `reg_check_plots()`'s replay all take the term through the existing `add_terms` seam, exactly as a `shape = "quadratic"` term does.

**Where it happens, and why there.** The pair is PARSED in S2 (block E2), so both parents reach `shape`, `multiplier`, `ref`/the anchor and the complete-case frame as ordinary variables — `shape = c(age = "quartiles")` on a crossed parent is what turns the nested arm into the cells arm, and it is the cure both refusals name. It is MATERIALISED at the very end of S5 (block Z), after the shape recode, after the anchor shift and **after the relevel** — which is what makes the combined factor's first level the pair of the parents' own references, so **`ref` needs no cross-specific grammar at all** (the study's P4, for free). The jamovi `reref` fast path is disabled under a cross for the same reason, and `crosses` joins both `jmvreg_fit_key(extra =)` lists: a nested arm's term is not a column, so `jmv_col_fp()` cannot see it and a stale hit would be a wrong table.

**The footer answers "is it real?" twice, with the same number.** The test is a **model comparison** with the additive counterpart, which is what covers both arms from one producer — a combined factor has no interaction TERM for `drop1()` to drop, yet it nests the additive model exactly. Measured against `anova(additive, crossed)` to **1e-10**. Cost, measured at n = 21 400: **+19 ms on a glm**, **+540 ms (ordinal)** and **+1 100 ms (multinomial)**, i.e. roughly a doubling of the fitting time for a 3+ level outcome — so per the maintainer's decision it joins the **default** `stats` set on a glm and is opt-in elsewhere, reusing `REG_CHECKS`' own free/refit vocabulary rather than inventing a rule. ⚠ that default **required a user-facing rename**: the `tab_vars` effect-modification test is `stats = "group_interaction"` now (`group_interact_lr` / `_f` / `_wald`), freeing `"interaction"` for the pair test — without it, putting `"interaction"` in the default set would have silently switched the `tab_vars` test on.

**Four defects found and fixed on the way, three of them beyond the two the study named.** (1) **C4-1** — `reg_global_rows()` compared *backticked* `term.labels` against bare names, so any variable whose name needs backticks lost its `Overall association (LR)` row silently, and `race × age4` is exactly that; it compares on the bare name and keeps `terms_i` verbatim for `drop1()`'s scope. (2) **C4-2** — `reg_tidy_rescale()`'s `td$term == v` is exact, so `multiplier` never reached `raceBlack:age` and a crossed slope printed a per-1-unit effect under a row labelled `per SD/17.3`; it matches a term whose `:`-split parts contain the variable, which leaves the squared term and the multinomial `term × y.level` behaviour untouched. (3) **`reg_compare_guard()` proves nesting from TERM LABELS**, and a combined factor's label contains neither parent's — so the headline "additive vs crossed" comparison degraded to Delta-AIC where a real LR test exists. It expands DECLARED crosses into their parents now (`reg_cross_expand_terms()`), and only declared ones: a hand-written `a:b` in a compound formula may genuinely not contain its main effects, and claiming otherwise would compute a bogus likelihood ratio. (4) **`reg_fit()`'s `drop_vars` ignored `add_terms`**, so a model's population was what `predictors` listed rather than what the formula uses — inert for a shape term (its variable is a predictor) but wrong for a crossed slope; it reads the terms' own variables now. Plus one message leak: `car::vif()` prints a note about higher-order terms on any interacted fit, describing a model the user asked for and offering nothing to act on — suppressed at the site.

**Two smaller decisions worth recording.** A nested block gets its own `Overall association (LR)` row — the joint test of its m slopes, the same question a factor block's row answers — through one declared term→block map (`reg_cross_term_var()`); and the crude nested fit's own `M` main effects are **not** poked into the moderator's block, which falls out of `reg_empirical_fit()`'s existing term filter rather than needing a guard.

**Four existing test contracts moved, and three of them were caught by the package's own guards rather than by review.** `test-jamovi-vocabulary.R` refused the new YAML option until it was declared UI-only — `crosses` folds into `predictors` exactly as `models` does, so it is not an argument of `tab_reg()` and had to say so. `test-non-ascii.R` refused `"race × age4"` written literally in the new test file (the `\uXXXX` rule covers `tests/` too, comments exempt). `test-test-rows.R` and `test-between-groups-gap.R` (6 assertions) pinned the old `interact_*` keys and the old `stats = "interaction"` spelling, which is precisely the rename this phase makes — updated, and they are what proves the tab_vars test still fires under its new key. `test-tab_reg-rr.R` pinned the default `stats` set, which now carries `"interaction"`.

**jamovi**: a hidden `crosses` Array of `Group{var1, var2}` in `jmvtabreg.a.yaml`, folded by `jmvtab_reg_cross_keys()` / `jmvtab_reg_cross_fold()` into `"a:b"` keys **appended to the predictors vector** — so the backend stays a pass-through and there is no second argument to keep in step; a model card that does not hold both parents is left alone, which is what makes with/without expressible from the "+" builder. `JMVREG_CACHE_SCHEMA` 6 → 7. The generated `.h.R` and JS are regenerated in **22g**, as declared; until then the option is inert and the module is correct.

**Documentation**: `?tab_reg`'s `@param predictors` gains the `:` rule, the two arms, the parent rule and the range caveat; `@param stats` gains both interaction keys with their cost; both regression vignettes gain a section (EN + FR) — how to read a cell row, the two arms, `shape = "quartiles"` as the route from a continuous predictor to the cell table, the footer test, the scale-dependence caveat (Ai & Norton), and the compound formula named as the **expert exit door** it is rather than as the way to write an interaction. One `NEWS.md` bullet, carrying the `:`-range and `stats`-key changes.

**The spelling is `a*b`, R's own, settled by a third follow-up question (§8.9 of the same doc).** `a:b` and `a*b` are not the same thing in R, and what tabxplor fits is always the FULL model — a combined factor spans `a + b + a:b`, the nested arm is `M/X` — so `a:b` would have named it correctly only half the time: measured, the two coincide for a factor pair (logLik −14142.9662 both) and diverge the moment a parent is continuous (−14505.62 against −14443.20), into exactly the origin-dependent model. `*` names it always, and it is what an R user already reads. `:` is now refused by NAME, a teaching error rather than a synonym — which also **removes the one cost the design carried**: `:` never had to be taken from tidyselect, because `*` does not collide with it. And the ORDER is presentation only: `race*age4` and `age4*race` are one fit (fitted values 2.6e-15 apart, same rank, same coefficient values renamed), differing in R only for the sequential Type-I `anova()` this package never uses (`drop1()` gives 8.286093 either way, the two-model LR p = 0.2178837 either way) — in tabxplor it says which variable the rows are about, so where only one parent is continuous the abort names the swap before the cure.

**A follow-up review asked whether the two refusals are really wanted, and the answer is written up as `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md` §8** (measured, with the literature). Both stand, and neither refuses a model a user can soundly ask for. For a categorical moderator, `a:b`, `a + a:b` and `a + b + a:b` are **ONE fit** — measured identical to the last digit (logLik −7580.837869 both ways, fitted values 1e-15) — so the parent rule refuses a *spelling*, and the alternative spelling's rows are a slope plus differences-of-slopes with no count, no crude twin and no reference row. The only genuinely different models it blocks are the ones that drop a continuous parent's main effect, and **every one of those depends on the anchor** — which since 22b-viii is a package default the user never set: re-fitting `married ~ age:tvhours` on a mean-centred `age` moves fitted **probabilities** by up to **0.55**, against 5e-16 for the invariant spelling. So the rule is the package's own mechanics, not a convention: *tabxplor fits only interaction models that are invariant to the anchoring of their continuous parents, because it anchors them.* Morris et al. (2023) name three cases where breaking marginality is right, and all three share a meaningful zero — which `ref = c(v = 0)` plus the formula hatch already expresses explicitly. **Both messages were rewritten to teach rather than refuse** (the parent rule now says the model is unchanged and only the rows differ; the continuous-moderator abort now names the formula hatch beside `shape`), and `?tab_reg` gained the continuous × continuous sentence. The two possible extensions are **Phase 22b-xii** below.

**Deferred, per the maintainer's decision**: the per-cell interaction COLOUR (the study's §4.15) — see the new phase below. Nothing structural is lost by waiting: it is one `MEASURES` row plus the nested-pair influence function, and the additive fit it needs is already computed for the test row.
