**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 8067** (7986 before; +81 from the tests added here, and the pre-existing over-dispersion WARN is gone with the parity fixtures it rode on). `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, three man pages rewritten with byte-identical `\usage` and identical `\item{}` name sets. Two snapshots moved, both audited line by line: `_snaps/golden.md` by exactly **3 CSS rules x 16 tables** (48 insertions, 0 deletions) and `_snaps/render-html.md` by **18 tooltip lines, every one of them a `ratio:` decimal**. ⚠ **not one `_golden/*.rds` moved**, which also measures the `ratio` floor change: no golden case builds a `display = "ratio"` column.

**THE CONSTANT ROW HOLDS THE QUANTITY THE COLUMN'S EFFECTS OPERATE ON.** That is the whole phase's first half, stated once as a new declared column, `EST_SCALES$const_display` (FK-checked): an odds ratio multiplies odds, so an odds column keeps the baseline **odds** with its probability as the cell's own aside (`1/1.19 (46%)`); a risk or rate ratio multiplies the LEVEL and a difference adds to it, so those show the level itself (`44%`, `45.7%`, `40.8`, `2.9`); a coefficient adds on the link scale (`-0.17`, `1.08`). One writer, `reg_constant_place()`, serves both producers -- `reg_column()`'s intercept and `reg_marginal_column()`'s g-computed baseline -- and it moves only the FIELD and the cell's own token, never the number.

**Why nothing else needed a branch.** On every non-odds scale the baseline then sits on a LEVEL token, which `format()`'s signing and multiplicative-glyph masks simply do not match -- so `+40.76`, `×2.79` and `÷2.30` disappear without a single new rule there. And because the estimate field is empty on that row, `display_write_col()`'s existing "stamp only where the primary is non-void" gate (22b-ii) leaves the cell alone, so `display` stays post-hoc and every `{est}`-based preset degrades correctly by construction. Exactly **one** clause was added to `format()`, for the log scales -- the only ones left on an additive token: *a regression baseline row is a level, not a comparison, so it never wears the sign*. Its multiplicative twin keeps its `at_one` guard, because there the rule REPLACES the value.

**And a level carries no test.** `pvalue = NA` wherever `const_display` is a level token, which extends 22b-viii's "no star on a predicted baseline" to the coefficient arm: `40.1%***` claimed the baseline risk differs from zero. `tab_constant_null()` needed no change at all -- it already keys on a finite p-value, so E2's "-- from 1 for the Constant --" aside now appears on exactly the tables that still test it. ⚠ one guard the first pass lacked: an **ordinal** cumOR has thresholds and no single intercept, so the placer stamps nothing where no baseline was computed and the row stays empty rather than printing the token's own NA.

**A summed score's RISK ratio was rendered as an ODDS ratio -- a real defect, and its cause was one overloaded row.** `reg_scale_of()` mapped BOTH `odds_ratio` and `pct_ratio` onto the single `score_ratio` scale, whose `est_field` is `or` and whose glyphs are the odds ratio's, so every summed-score RR printed `1/x` and wrote into the wrong field. Split into **`score_odds_ratio`** (today's row) and a new **`score_ratio`** (`est_field = "ratio"`, `label_meas = "ratio"`, `break_key = "pct_ratio"`), exactly mirroring `odds_ratio` / `pct_ratio` -- the same move 22a-iii made for the ungrouped RR. `REG_SCALE_GROUPED` and `REG_EMPIRICAL$grouped_binomial` point at the two, and a summed score's RR now reads `÷1.3` on its own ladder, its baseline the mean SCORE.

**Digits.** `REG_CELL_DIGITS`: `mean_ratio` / `raw_diff` / `mean_diff` 2 -> 1, and `DISPLAY_TOKENS$ratio$min_digits` 2 -> 1 (`or` stays 2). `odds_ratio` 0 and `score_odds_ratio` 2 stay: one `digits` serves every token of a cell, so lowering the score scale would turn `1/1.20` into `1/1.2`. One inconsistency fixed on the way -- an `obs` / `gap` floored at a hard-coded 2 while its model twin floored at the token's value, so a crude ratio printed `(×1.43)` beside a modelled `×1.2`; it reads the column's own `est_display` floor now, which is the same comparison at the same precision.

**A CONTINUOUS PREDICTOR'S LEVEL IS COMPOSED, not written three times.** The old code wrote the shape label and then **overwrote** it with the unit, so `log`/`sqrt` were invisible under the default `multiplier` -- reachable only with `multiplier = 1`, which is why the test passed and `man/tab_reg.Rd` promised the opposite. One composer now builds the whole string: `log(x), per 0.39 (SD), at 3.78 (mean)`. The shape mark comes from the KIND (a new `REG_SHAPE_MARKS`, with a literal `x` because the `var` column already names the variable), the unit from a restructured `reg_multiplier_value()` returning the value and its keyword separately, the anchor from `reg_anchor_word()`. `reg_shape_apply()`'s `labels` output is **deleted** with the `sub()` pass it fed, and `shared` carries the kinds instead. French re-merged (`par %s` / `à %s`); `msgmerge` fuzzy-matched the retired `"(at %s)"`, so its parentheses were stripped by hand.

**THE SPARKLINE IS DRAWN TO SCALE, and three reported problems fall out of that one change.** Its bins are equal-COUNT, so one glyph per bin plots the curve against RANK -- and a monotone `shape` leaves rank order untouched, which is exactly why the same curve came out for identity, log and sqrt. `rd_spark()` now takes the CURVE and interpolates it (`stats::approx`) onto a fixed 10-cell grid equally spaced in the SHAPED variable's own units, clamped to the central 95 % of x (two columns `rd_bin()` carries -- ⚠ columns, not an attribute: the curve is `mutate()`d, bound per `tab_vars` group and sliced again before it is drawn, and only a column survives all three). This is what every standard linearity diagnostic does (component+residual, empirical-logit plots) and what `reg_panel_linearity()` already did; the panel is untouched. Measured on `married ~ age`: identity `▁▆██████▇▆`, log `▁▄▆██████▆`, sqrt `▁▅▇█████▇▆`. The glyph count is now constant, so the svg width is too: `dx` 9 -> 5 and `lwd` 2.8 -> 2.4 give **47.4 px for every predictor**, where `age` drew 83.8 and `tvhours` 38.8.

**The N came back as a footer row, and the baseline's own base became a decision.** `TEST_ROWS$n$render` `"record"` -> `"grid"` -- one word. The Constant's count left the family-free counter for `reg_constant_count()`, which needs the CONTRAST to know what its base even is: the model N under `marginal` (the row IS the population), the **reference profile's own count** where every predictor is categorical (a real subgroup -- and a 0 there would warn that the baseline rests on nobody), nothing where a continuous predictor makes the profile a place nobody is.

**Interactions.** The block is **named as it was typed** -- `age*tvhours`, the `predictors` key itself; `reg_cross_label()` and its `mult_sign` use are deleted, and the var column, both footer rows and `reg_formulas()` now agree with the call. A nested slope row reads `age per 13.5 (SD) — [0,1)`: the modified variable opens it, an em dash separates it from the moderator level, and no anchor clause (a nested slope does not depend on one). ⚠ `reg_cross_sep()` keeps serving the CELLS arm, where it is part of a materialised factor's LEVELS -- data, not a label.

**Two interaction defects, both reproduced before being fixed.** (1) The tooltip read `age × tvhours: mean NA (SD NA); mean if yes NA, if no NA`: `reg_spec_tips_num()` described the cross KEY, which is not a column at all. It resolves a block to the numeric variable its rows are ABOUT -- the modified parent for a nested block -- and tests that on the FRAME rather than on `numeric_preds`, since a crossed slope's parent is supplied by the interaction term and is never listed among the model's own predictors. It also emits no row where the statistics are not finite, which is the general rule the maintainer asked for: *a tooltip never shows a field it does not have*. (2) A nested slope row printed an adjusted proportion that was the moderator level's own -- already on the moderator's row, and disagreeing with it (38 % beside 39 %). A slope has no level pair, so `reg_fill_base()` now skips those rows, exactly as it does for an ordinary numeric predictor.

**HTML: the first column, and a long block name.** A **row_var separator no longer crosses the variable-name column**: a rowspanned name cell is anchored in its block's first row and escapes `tr.tx-bb2>*` anyway, while a ONE-ROW block's cell is a direct child of the closing row and drew a rule its neighbours did not -- `tx-nb`, emitted on exactly the name cells that should draw none, opts them all out. The **model-fit block** is a boundary between two KINDS of block, so it does cross: `tx-bt2` on its first row and `tx-bb2` on its label cell, 2 px like every other column, where both were 1 px. ⚠ the decision lives in the RENDERER (which knows what a cell is) and the CSS is one dumb rule -- a name cell carries `tx-nb` or a boundary class, never both, which is what keeps the exemption from having to out-specify the cell-scoped rules. And a rotated `age*tvhours` **breaks before its operator**, at render time only: `tab_wrap_text()` cannot do it (it breaks on spaces, and turns the ones it keeps into narrow NO-BREAK ones), and `*` is not a legal character in an R name, so in a name cell it can only be the cross operator.

**VIF and dfbetas are MARKED, and the answer to the question is that no threshold is a test.** `REG_CHECKS` gained a `flag` on the two gof checks -- collinearity >= 10 (the textbook figure; O'Brien 2007 argues explicitly against any such cut-off) and |dfbetas| >= 1 (Belsley-Kuh-Welsch's small-sample rule, the one that stays meaningful at survey n, where their 2/sqrt(n) flags thousands of points). So the mark wears the **faintest** under-shade -- "look at this" -- never the p-value's deepest one, per the maintainer's call. It is carried by one new `DISPLAY_TOKENS` row, `gof_warn`, the `gof` token's colourable twin: the console reads the palette's own slot 5 through `cli::make_ansi_style()` (not `cli::col_red()`), and html / markdown / Excel go through one new arm of `fmt_color_slots()`. ⚠ `under_slots` carries a leading 0, so the faintest shade is the smallest POSITIVE slot, never `min()`. The four `"gof"` literals outside those bodies read a derived `DISPLAY_GOF_TOKENS` instead, so a third sibling would need no edit; the two inside `get_num()` / `set_num()` stay literal, because the round-trip assertion scans those bodies for token names.

**Three defects found and fixed on the way.** (1) The regression footer was forced **black and bold** per ROW (Phase 14q), which would have painted the new mark black; the rule is now per CELL, and a `gof_warn` keeps its shade -- the black-and-bold rule is about not GREYING a model-fit number, not about refusing the one signal the footer carries. (2) A **transposed** table crashed on the new footer boundary (`subscript out of bounds`): a row-index fact of the original table means nothing after the flip, where the footer is a set of COLUMNS. The transpose drops it, and the engine bound-checks anyway. (3) `reg_level_counts()`' header claimed the Constant showed the model N; it now says where that decision lives.

**Accepted, and worth knowing.** A crosstab `display = "ratio"` column and its tooltips print one decimal (`×1.3`, not `×1.29`) -- the same floor the maintainer asked for on the regression side, and the only reason `_snaps/render-html.md` moved. `n = "no"` still takes the sparkline with it (there is then no cell to draw it in). And a nested slope row states no anchor, so on a model where a continuous variable appears ONLY inside a cross, its anchor is visible nowhere.



##### Phase 22b-xi — the interaction colour: NOT IMPLEMENTED

The study's §4.15, deferred by decision G4 of 22b-ix. Once an interaction is a predictor, the two-channel colour language has a second thing to say about each cell, and it needs **no new `fmt` field**: the **text** grades the cell's own effect against the reference cell (the ordinary measure), the **background** grades how far the cell departs from **no interaction at all**, greyed by `color_signif` when that departure could be chance.

The no-interaction expectation is the ADDITIVE model's estimate for that cell — and that model is already fitted, for 22b-ix's `Interaction (LR)` footer row. So the measure has exactly the shape `color = "adjustment"` already has (`obs` = the value compared to, `est` = the value shown, `gap_se` = the SE of their difference), and both legs are nested fits on one frame, which is the situation `reg-influence.R` already solves. **One new `MEASURES` row**, routed through the existing nested-pair machinery so the design-based case comes for free.

Why it is worth its own phase, and what to weigh first: a cell's own stars answer *"is this cell different from the REFERENCE cell?"* — mostly the two main effects talking — while this answers *"does this cell depart from what those main effects alone predict?"*, which is what an interaction table is for. Against it: k×m per-cell departure tests are multiple comparisons on a quantity the footer already summarises once, and it spends the background channel. Two things come at no extra cost if it lands: the **additive-scale** departure is the same measure under `measure = "difference"`, and a **RERI** footer row is one more `TEST_ROWS` entry from the same two fits.

##### Phase 22b-xii-a — the two automatic behaviours + `shape = "sd_bands"`

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 8085** (8018 before). `devtools::document()` clean, NAMESPACE unchanged; `man/tab_reg.Rd` keeps a byte-identical `\usage` and its only new `\item{}` is the documented `"sd_bands"` value. No golden and no snapshot moved. Grounded in `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md` **§8.11**.

**Two refusals became two automatic behaviours, and they are NOT the same kind of decision** — which is what shaped both. **The swap is free**: `race*age` has exactly one table that can exist (only a continuous variable has slopes within groups) and `*` is symmetric in the fit, so reading it as `age*race` decides nothing statistical. It swaps, says so in one line, and the block is named as the swap. **The cut is not free**: `age*tvhours` has no cells, so the moderator is cut into quartiles — but that changes the FIT, and the `Interaction (LR)` row moves by **13x** across bin counts nobody chose (p = 0.00068 at four groups against 0.00859 at three), with an outright conclusion flip on `married ~ tvhours*age` (0.0013 continuous against 0.0651 at three). So it happens — a table beats an error — but **stated in one line, never silent**, with both ways out named. It is decided where `shape` is RESOLVED and before it is applied (S2, block G), the one point that can answer "will this still be continuous?", which is also what makes an unnamed fallback (`shape = 3`) win by itself.

**`shape = "sd_bands"`: four bands, and the measurement chose the number.** Cuts at the mean and one SD either side — moderated regression's own low/medium/high landmarks (Aiken & West) used as BOUNDARIES. Per cent per band on a normal variable: 16/34/34/16; three bands leave **64–68 %** in one undifferentiated row, five empty a band on anything skewed (measured on age, tvhours, lognormal, exponential). ⚠ **unlike quantiles the bands are not balanced**, and a landmark outside the data is DROPPED rather than asked of `cut()` — an exponential gets three bands, not four — so the docs name quantiles where group sizes matter. The mean is always strictly inside the range of a variable that varies, so the only reachable abort is one that does not. Labels carry both facts as asked: `[29.89,47.18) m-sd..m`.

**One defect found and fixed on the way, pre-existing and general.** `tab_html()` escaped column headers but **not row labels**, so an ordinary level like `Arts & Humanities` emitted a raw `&` and `<25 years` a raw `<` — invalid html since the beginning. The generic cell path passes `esc = identity`, right for an fmt cell (which carries our own `<span>` / `<svg>`) and wrong for a character column, which is user data; non-fmt columns are escaped now. The new band labels would have been the first to hit it by construction. Also: adding a `shape` value made `jamovi/js/jmvtabreg.js`'s generated vocabulary block stale — the `test-jamovi-vocabulary.R` guard caught it and `dev/generate_jamovi_js.R` regenerated it (one line).

**Still open from 22b-xii**: the *coefficient* route — one row for the bare product with `multiplier` as `k_a x k_b` — is NOT implemented, and remains the entry below. The cut now covers the friendliness half of that phase.

##### Phase 22b-xii — a continuous x continuous interaction, if it is wanted: NOT IMPLEMENTED

Studied and grounded in `dev/reg_interactions_and_predictor_terms.md` **section 8** (measured on real data, with the literature). The refusal stands as the DEFAULT — `shape = c(b = "quartiles")` gives a strictly more informative table than any alternative, and the formula hatch already fits the model correctly and anchored. Two extensions exist if the classical table is wanted anyway, in increasing cost:

- **a third arm, `both_numeric`** — model `a + b + a:b` (the only origin-invariant spelling), ONE interaction row, with `multiplier` applied as `k_a x k_b` so it reads `1/1.07` per SD x SD instead of the unreadable `1.00` the hatch prints. It reuses the `add_terms` seam and the skeleton's numeric branch; the footer test needs nothing. The row carries no count, no `{base}` and no `Obs_*`, which must be documented rather than discovered. ⚠ **precondition**: `reg_tidy_rescale()` applies ONE `k` per term, so a term whose two parts BOTH carry a multiplier would silently take the last one — it needs the product. Unreachable today (the arm aborts, and `multiplier` is off in formula mode), so it is a landmine to defuse before the arm lands, not a live bug.
- **simple slopes at declared moderator values** — the genuinely tabxplor-shaped answer and the one the literature recommends (Aiken & West; Johnson-Neyman): rows at `mean -/+ SD`, or at values named through `ref`'s own grammar, each an effect the colour engine and the stars already understand. 22b-viii's anchor plus `at_reference`'s datagrid are most of the machinery. It cannot carry counts or an observed companion — those rows describe nobody as a group.

##### Phase 22b-xiii — regression framework statistical stress test and corrections

A full review of `tab_reg()`'s statistical framework has landed in `dev/reg_math_review_edge_cases.md`. **Read it in full before planning either sub-phase**: its §1.3 is the findings table, §2-7 hold one root cause and one reproduction each, §8 lists what was measured SOUND (do not "fix" those), §9.3 the three invariants. Findings are keyed `A1`-`A3` / `B1`-`B2` / `C1`-`C4` there (`B3` was raised then withdrawn — see below); the sub-phases below use the same keys.

⚠ **The inference-basis ladder — recall it before touching any interval, and never mix its rungs.** `svy_inference_basis()` (`R/survey-design.R:109`) returns exactly one of three states, and what is statistically right differs at each:

| rung      | reached when                                 | what the crude closed form assumes                                          | verdict of the review                  |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `n`       | no `wt`, no design (an ordinary `tab_reg()`) | i.i.d. rows                                                                 | exact — hand-checked vs Woolf / Katz   |
| `weights` | a `wt` column                                | a design at `ids = ~1`: weights, **no clusters, no strata, no calibration** | exact — 0.03 % from `svyglm(ids = ~1)` |
| `design`  | a `svydesign` passed as `data`               | still independence across PSUs — **false as soon as clusters exist**        | 28 % narrow to 2.2x wide (§5)          |

Two consequences to carry. The independence assumption the crude closed form makes is **correct at the first two rungs**, so nothing there is to be "fixed" — the defect is specific to a real cluster design. And `tab_reg()` has no "weights without design effect" state: `reg-empirical.R:153` and `tab_reg.R:2832` pass `force = TRUE`, so any `wt` lands on `weights` whatever `options(tabxplor.design_effect)` says, unlike `tab()`. `design_partial` is `design` degraded and follows it.

**Decisions taken with the maintainer (2026-08-20)** — implement them, do not re-derive or widen them.

- **G5 — the crude interval is refit from the univariable design-based fit at the `design` rung ONLY.** At `n` and `weights` the closed form stays, its independence assumption being true there. The machinery already exists: the numeric-predictor arm calls `reg_empirical_fit()` today. Measured: the point estimate does not move at all, only the width.
- **G6 — a non-identified estimate renders as an unbounded marker, not as a number.** `>1000` (and its inverse form), star stripped. **No message — the marker IS the message.** No new dependency, no penalised refit.
- **G7 — one reference distribution per table, taken from the fit.** The marginal / at-reference / Constant finalisers stop hard-coding `qnorm` and call the same `reg_wald_crit()` the coefficient path already calls, so the rule is one function with no rung-specific branch: dispersion known → z (an unweighted binomial is unchanged), otherwise t on `df.residual(fit)`. Immaterial at the `n` and `weights` rungs (t(n-p) vs z is under 0.1 % beyond n = 200); the real correction at the `design` rung, where `df.residual(svyglm)` is `degf + 1 - p` and can be 17. G5 fixes the crude half of the same inconsistency for free, a refit crude column carrying its own `df.residual`.

**Nothing is owed to 22g**: none of this adds, removes or renames a `tab_reg()` argument or a jamovi option, so no `jmvtools::prepare()` is required. **Deferred to 22h / 23a**: the vignette prose for the design-rung crude interval and for the unbounded marker — the legend text itself is part of the fix and lands here.

**Testing budget** (Phase 23e wants the suite under 20 s): the §9.3 invariants are the right guard, but the 55-combination sweep that found these defects takes minutes. Fold a **small representative grid** into the existing regression test files and keep the exhaustive sweep as a `dev/` harness, never a testthat file.

###### Phase 22b-xiii-1 — the estimand a cell claims

`A1` `A2` `A3` `C4` — everything where the printed number, its interval or its scale is not the estimand the column declares. One context: `prob_effect()` and the `REG_EMPIRICAL` declarations in `R/reg-empirical.R`, plus the three Wald finalisers in `R/tab_reg.R`. No survey machinery involved.

The four defects share one theme worth settling in the plan before fixing them one by one: **a shape's own declaration is currently decorative in three places** — `prob_effect()` re-derives the arm from `fam$coef` instead of from the shape (`A2`), the marginal finalisers derive `do_exp` from the internal comparison key instead of from the estimand's declared `scale` (`A3`), and `reg_same_estimand()` compares `scale` alone, which cannot separate two `log_coef` columns (`C4` — the guard that should have caught `A2`). Making the dispatch read what the fact tables already declare is the simplification; patching each symptom is not.

⚠ **`B3` is WITHDRAWN — do not "fix" it** (review §7.1, and this is the rule the whole phase turns on). The crude risk difference uses plain Wald where `tab(ci =)` uses Newcombe, and that is **correct**: D22 requires the crude column to carry the univariable model's own interval, the model column for `measure = "difference"` is an identity-link binomial, and its Wald interval is bit-identical to the crude one to 8 digits. Woolf is Wald on the log OR, Katz is Wald on the log RR, plain Wald is Wald on the RD — three faces of one rule. Newcombe is a score interval no GLM produces, so adopting it would make the risk difference the one estimand whose crude column stopped mirroring its twin. The tooltip claim was false too: `reg-empirical.R:284` passes the family's declared method and says so in a comment. **Read this before touching any `ci_method`: a crude engine is chosen to match the model's, never on its own statistical merits.**

Then the §9.3 invariants, which is what makes the whole class non-recurring: an interval contains its estimate; a reference cell equals its scale's neutral; a star agrees with its interval.

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 8329** (8085 before; +244 from the tests added here). `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged, and not one `man/*.Rd`, `_golden/*.rds` or `_snaps` file moved** — which is the phase's own claim tested: nothing here touches `tab()`, and no golden case builds a `tab_reg()` table.

**ONE ROOT, NOT FOUR DEFECTS: a shape's declaration was decorative in three places.** `prob_effect()` re-derived which arithmetic to run from the crude FAMILY's coefficient shape; the marginal finalisers derived "exponentiate?" from the internal `marginaleffects` comparison key rather than from the estimand's declared `exp`; and `reg_same_estimand()` — the guard that should have caught both — compared only `scale`, which every logged measure shares. Making each dispatch read what the fact tables already declare is a **net deletion**: `reg_marginal_column()` goes 97 → 65 deparsed lines and the two files are 32 code lines shorter, with `EST_SCALES` untouched.

**A1 — a multinomial crude estimate outside its own interval.** The estimate is category *j* against the PIVOT (the reference outcome category, `nnet::multinom`'s own estimand); the interval was built from `(1 - prop)`, i.e. *j* against everything else. Two estimands in one cell. The grid already carried the pivot's weighted count in `emp_wpos` / `emp_wneg` — and **both were dead**, declared and written but read nowhere — so they are replaced by the two SHARES the interval needs (`emp_pivot_prop`, `emp_ref_pivot_prop`), and the Woolf arm becomes one uniform 2x2 with no branch. On a binary or `share`-mode outcome the pivot IS the complement, so it reduces to today's form exactly: the unification is the fix, not a special case. Measured on `party3 ~ race`: all four cells now equal the hand `ci_or()` on the {j, pivot} x {level, ref level} table to the last digit, where three of four previously printed an estimate outside its bracket. ⚠ `emp_ratio`'s own arithmetic is deliberately untouched — rewriting it in terms of the shares is algebraically identical but moves the last ulp, and the parity tests pin those values.

**A2 — `Obs_log(RR)` was log(OR) with a Woolf interval, and it was BROADER than the review found.** `base_sh <- fam[[fam$coef]]` is deleted; the dispatch reads the shape's own scale geometry, then its own `ci_method`. Besides the reported `grouped_binomial$rr_log`, this hit **any borrowed logged shape whose block differs from the crude key** — plain `binomial` x `marginal`/`at_reference` x `log_risk`, whose shape lives in `REG_EMPIRICAL$rr` while the family in hand is `binomial`. Measured on the `tea` battery: `Obs_log(RR)` = -0.178809 with the hand Katz interval and p, against `Obs_log(OR)` = -0.309712 — two numbers that were one. **A latent twin went with it**: the difference arm read `fam$method_diff`, the crude key's block again; it reads `emp_method(sh)` now. Every reachable `ame` shape declares `"wald"`, so behaviour is unchanged today, and `method_diff` keeps its one honest reader — the grid's own level-vs-reference difference, a descriptive quantity belonging to no estimand.

**A3 — one flag was doing two jobs.** `reg_estimand()`'s logged branch sets `exp <- FALSE` and `scale <- "log_coef"` but deliberately leaves `comparison` alone, because the engine still has to work on the log; the marginal path then derived `do_exp` from `comparison` and exponentiated the ratio back onto a column stamped `log_coef`. Split everywhere into **`log_ratio`** (what the ENGINE computes — drives `reg_gcomp_maker(ratio =)`, the `marginaleffects` comparison string and its label parser) and **`do_exp`** (what the COLUMN prints — `log_ratio && exponentiate`, read from the estimand's own `exp`). Measured: a `log(mRR)` column is now the exact `log()` of its `mRR` twin, estimate, both bounds and p, on the model AND the crude column; the reference cell holds `0` where it held `1`; the interval is symmetric Wald instead of Wald-on-the-log. `reg_empirical_fit()` passes `exponentiate = FALSE`, which **deletes** its manual re-log — its contract was always the native scale.

**And `reg_marginal_column()` stopped hard-coding.** Its five `shape` arms each fixed the estimate field, the reference neutral, `ref =` and `ci_method`; only one read `EST_SCALES[[sc]]$est_field`, and the `raw_ratio` arm wrote into `ratio` even where the scale said `diff`. They are **one** `do.call(fmt, ...)` driven by the scale — `est_field`, `neutral`, `mult` (which decides both `wald_log` and the `ref = "1"` marker) and `sd_from` — which is exactly what the function's own comment already claimed. The `shape` argument is deleted; `reg_cols_vsrest()` passes `scale =` like its sibling, which also fixes its silent `sc = "odds_ratio"` under a logged estimand. Verified arm by arm: `reg_pct_type()` returns `"none"` off a pct scale, which is `fmt()`'s own default, so it is passed uniformly; `sd_from == "var"` is TRUE on `raw_diff` and on nothing else these arms touch.

**The Constant row of a logged column** (maintainer's decision): `log(baseline)` on the column's own scale, not a hole. `log_coef` is ONE row shared by every logged measure, so a link-scale column cannot say on its own whether its exponential is an odds or a level — and the baseline differs by exactly that. `reg_estimand()`'s synthesised branch records **`log_of`** (the scale it is the log OF) beside the `display` member it already synthesised; `reg_exp_scale_of()` reads it through the summed-score remap; `reg_constant_baseline(log = TRUE)` builds the cell on the exponentiated twin's scale and logs the three numbers after — so the interval stays exact and `reg_constant_cell()` needs no arm of its own. Verified both ways: a logged risk ratio's Constant is `log()` of its twin's baseline LEVEL, a logged odds ratio's is `log()` of its twin's baseline ODDS.

**C4 — one predicate, four callers.** `reg_same_estimand(shape, scale, est)` compares the scale AND the declared measure **word**, which is what tells `log(OR)` from `log(RR)` on the single `log_coef` scale. Taking the scale as an argument rather than off a column is what finally lets `reg_color_notes()` — which asks the same question before any column exists — use the shared function instead of its own inline copy, something its comment had been asking for. Swept over the whole grid: every reachable `(family, effect, measure)` pairs its crude shape's word, so the clause refuses nothing that works.

**Three further live defects found and fixed, none in the review.** (1) `reg_empirical_columns()`'s marginal override wrote `emp_ratio_prop` / `emp_diff` over the estimate — a **no-op** for the two cases it was written for (multinomial `marginal` x `difference` and x `ratio` already produce exactly those through `prob_effect()`), and **wrong** for `at_reference` x `odds_ratio`, where `marginal` is TRUE and `ratio_marg` FALSE, so it wrote a risk DIFFERENCE into the `or` field of an `odds_ratio` column. Deleted. (2) `reg_crude_shape()`'s `%||% fam[[fam$coef]]` fallback substituted a different estimand for a missing declaration; deleted, so a miss now degrades to **no** crude column (`reg_empirical_columns()` already treats NULL that way). (3) Two shapes were genuinely missing — `multinomial$ame_ratio_log` and `ordinal$ame_ratio_log` — which is what made multinomial/ordinal marginal-log fall through that fallback onto an un-logged OR; declared now.

**The guard is a foreign key, checked at load** (maintainer's decision). The existing `crude_shape` edge tests membership in the UNION of every block's shape names, so `ame_ratio_log` would have passed it while resolving nowhere. The new edge qualifies the key by its block (`"grouped_binomial.rr_log"`) and enumerates what every reachable estimand actually asks for — both `trials` states, and the `_log` twin `reg_estimand()` composes by string concatenation. **26 reachable keys, all resolving.** A missing declaration now fails the install, at the moment it is made.

**`REG_EMPIRICAL$*$coef_log` is deleted**: declared on all eight blocks and read nowhere, it existed only to serve the `base_sh` indirection this phase removes.

**Verification.** Three invariants, read off each column's own declared scale so one loop covers every producer: an interval contains its estimate, a reference cell IS the scale's neutral, a star agrees with its interval. `tests/testthat/test-reg-invariants.R` runs the light grid the maintainer chose — 10 cases, one per family plus the two logged contrasts and a summed score, on a 2 000-row subset, each with `empirical = "column"` so model and crude columns are both swept (**198 assertions, 4.7 s**, well under the slowest file). `dev/verify_reg_invariants.R` is the exhaustive sweep: 7 outcomes x 3 contrasts x 7 measure spellings x 2 `empirical` modes — **399 built columns, 1 475 cells, zero invariant failures and zero untyped errors**, with 120 typed refusals. Targeted regressions went to the files that own each area (A1 → `test-tab_reg-empirical.R` against the hand 2x2; A2 → `test-tab_reg-rr.R` against hand Katz, on both the summed-score and the borrowed-shape path; the logged baseline → `test-reg-baseline.R`; the qualified edge → `test-fact-keys.R`; C4's grid → the invariants file).

⚠ **One test of mine went vacuous and was caught before it landed**: the A1 regression parsed the crude column name as `Obs_OR_<cat>` where the package emits `Obs_<cat> vs <pivot>`, so every comparison was skipped and only the "there is at least one column" assertion fired. It now counts the comparisons it makes and asserts the count — a cheap habit for any test that loops over discovered names.

**Two premises corrected on the way, neither a defect.** `?tab_reg`'s `@param measure` already said a `log_*` spelling is "the same fit, un-exponentiated"; that was true of the coefficient path and FALSE of the marginal one, so the page needed no edit — the code now matches what it always promised. And a crude column's modelled level is the outcome's FIRST level (`tab_reg()`'s documented default), which is what a hand-computed comparison must use.

**Accepted, and flagged rather than fixed.** An ORDINAL crude column's reference row carries `NA` rather than its scale's neutral, on every measure: those rows come from a univariable `polr` refit whose tidy has no reference term, and `reg_fit_overlay()` writes only the rows the fit produced. It is a hole, not a wrong number, and it is symmetric across the logged and un-logged spellings; the invariants skip a non-finite estimate for exactly this reason.


###### Phase 22b-xiii-2 — what a number's uncertainty means

`B1` `B2` `C1` `C2` `C3` — the number is right, the uncertainty or the identifiability attached to it is not. One context: the design boundary (`R/survey-design.R`, `R/survey-variance.R`, the design path of `R/reg-empirical.R`), the critical-value plumbing in `R/tab_reg.R`, and the gap rendering in `R/fmt_class.R`.

`B1` (G5) and `C1` (G7) are the substance and are best done together, G5 giving the crude column its own `df.residual` and so settling half of what G7 unifies. Budget the plan for the performance question G5 raises — one extra `svyglm` per factor predictor per model, at the `design` rung only — and for the legend, which must then stop naming a df no column used.

`C2` and `C3` are small and self-contained. `reg_gap_se_of()` recovers a SE by dividing by z an interval that was built with t, inflating it by exactly `t(df)/z` (+31 % at df = 5): recover with the column's own critical value, then test with z if that convention is kept, the two decisions being independent and currently conflated. And a pinned gap bound renders as `-0.0`, which reads as "just excludes the null" when it IS the null — a presentation fix; the folding arithmetic behind it is sound and documented.

`B2` (G6) closes the phase: detect non-identification on the fitted values, render the unbounded marker, strip the star. It needs the display grammar, which `C3` has just put in context.

⚠ **Inherited from 22b-xiii-1, reported not fixed**: `reg_crude_if_maker()` (`R/reg-influence.R:130-131`) builds the crude leg's influence function on a category-**vs-rest** indicator, while a multinomial crude odds ratio is category-**vs-pivot** (which 22b-xiii-1 made the interval honour too). It is currently unreachable — a conditional odds-ratio gap is refused as non-collapsible, and the marginal shapes really are vs-rest — so it is a landmine rather than a wrong number, and it belongs with the gap SE.

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 8376** (8329 before; +47 from the tests added here). `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, and **not one `man/*.Rd`, `_golden/*.rds` or `_snaps` file moved** — nothing here touches `tab()`, and no golden case builds a `tab_reg()` table.

**ONE IDEA, APPLIED THREE TIMES: an interval must say which model and which reference distribution it came from, and every consumer must read that back off the column.** That is what makes the four findings one phase rather than four patches — and each fix is a fact moved to where it was already needed, never a new mechanism.

**B2 / G6 is ABANDONED, and that is the maintainer's call recorded rather than an omission.** No unbounded marker, no `>1000`, no star stripped: a twelve-digit odds ratio is how every regression package reports non-identification, and a reader infers the problem from the value itself. Nothing was implemented. (The alternative offered and declined was a purely value-derived marker in `format()` — no fit fact, no digest member, no cache-schema bump — which would additionally have covered the crude column's `0` / `Inf` cells that fitted-value detection structurally cannot reach.)

**B1 / G5 — the change is ONE PREDICATE, because the alternative route already existed.** `reg_crude_saturated()` answers *"is the univariable model's interval available in closed form?"* and asked only whether the model was saturated. It now also asks whether the closed form's own assumption holds: every engine here reads a `1/a+1/b+1/c+1/d`-style variance, which assumes the two compared groups are INDEPENDENT. Weights alone do not break that — a flat design IS a weight vector — but clusters, strata and calibration do, and the sign of the dropped covariance is invisible in the number (§5.2 measured 28 % too narrow in one direction and 2.2× too wide in the other). So the predicate gained a third clause and `svy_design_structured()` was named once in `R/survey-variance.R`, beside the `svy_design_is_flat()` it negates — `reg_empirical()`'s `need_svy` was that same expression written out, and now reads it. Everything else was already there: `reg_empirical_fit()` fits through the table's own `reg_fit()` (so `svyglm` / `svyolr` / `svyVGAM` come for free) and `emit()` → `reg_fit_overlay()` already splices fit-derived rows on every arm, so the behavioural change is widening one vector, `fit_preds_e`.

**Measured**: under a clustered design `Obs_OR`'s estimate, both bounds and its p are now **`confint(svyglm(y ~ x, design))` to 1e-9** — it is not "close to" the univariable design-based fit any more, it IS it. A **flat** `svydesign(ids = ~1)` keeps the closed form, so it still tells the same story as the `wt =` table, and the weights rung is byte-identical.

**Three consequences carried with it, each a stamp that had to stop lying.** The crude column stamps its MODEL twin's `ci_method` (`wald` / `wald_log` / `profile`) rather than `woolf`, which is what keeps the pair in one legend block — and the "(Katz closed form)" rider disappears on its own, because the two bodies now match. `n_eff` goes NA: the field IS "the effective sample size used for this cell's CI", and no base was used. And the gap-SE loop flips with the same predicate — `closed_form` goes FALSE, so the `fits_crude` loop, which already "covers FACTOR predictors too", picks them up; the two loops stay disjoint by construction because they read one fact.

**Cost, measured** (`dev/benchmarks/results_2.0.0/phase22b-xiii-2_design_crude_refit.txt`; n = 20 000, 200 PSUs in 4 strata, 3 factor predictors + 1 numeric): **+131 ms** on a coefficient table and **+175 ms** on a marginal one, against a `weights`-rung build of the same table — i.e. ~30 % of the build, on a path only a real survey design reaches.

**A LIVE DEFECT the refit depended on, found while verifying and not in the review.** A multinomial crude column left every NUMERIC predictor's row completely empty: `reg_empirical_fit()`'s coefficient branch stamped `category = ""` while `emit()` looks its rows up under the outcome category, so `cat_get()` missed and every fit-derived row was silently dropped. Reproduced on `party3 ~ race + age` (`Obs_*` showed `race Black 0.098 [0.086;0.113]` beside `age NA NA`); the branch now carries `td$y.level` where the tidy has one, and the row equals the univariable `multinom` coefficient. The marginal branch was unaffected (it already carried `a$group`) and ordinal too (one column, key `""`) — both verified. **Part 1 could not land without it**: a multinomial factor predictor's refit would have spliced nothing and silently kept the plug-in.

**C1 / G7 — one reference distribution per FIT, and it needed no new fact, only one that stopped being thrown away.** `reg_fit()` already computed `disp_known` and `df.residual(fit)` and discarded them; it returns them now, mirroring `reg_build_digest()`, which has carried both since 15b — so **`JMVREG_CACHE_SCHEMA` does not move**. The three finalisers that hard-coded `qnorm` now call the one `reg_wald_crit()`: `reg_marginal_gcomp()` (threading `disp_known` / `df` into `reg_wald_finalize()` too, so bounds and p stay duals), `reg_constant_baseline()` (whose `reg_constant_cell()` already took `crit` as a formal), and `reg_marginal_me()` — which had **no** critical value at all, taking `marginaleffects`' own z bounds while never reading the `std.error` beside them. It rebuilds from estimate + SE now through one local `refer()` closure, which also folds the `exp()` both its arms were doing by hand. `reg_wald_crit()` itself became the fit's own arm of `conf_level_to_crit()`, so an absent df degrades to z through `df_clean()` instead of propagating NA. **The 3+ level engines stay on z, deliberately and documented**: `multinom` / `polr` / `svy_vglm` / `svyolr` define no residual df and their own summaries report z, so those tables are internally consistent.

**Each column now STAMPS the df it used** (`reg_wald_degf()`: NA where the reference is z, NA under `profile`, whose LR bounds refer to no distribution at all), and `reg_finalize()` stamps **none** — the df is not a table fact. Measured on a 24-PSU / 4-strata design: every column of the model's own fit (estimate, marginal sweep, baseline row) carries `df.residual(svyglm)`, and the crude column carries the weakest of its OWN univariable fits, which is legitimately larger (fewer parameters). One reference per fit, not per table — which is the correction the review asked for, stated more precisely than it was asked.

**And the df left the colour legend for the `Model:` footer.** `legend_method_phrase()` is part of the legend's GROUPING key, so a per-column number would split the very crude/adjusted block 22a-ii exists to produce; the clause is gated `!is_reg` (crosstabs are byte-identical) and the footer names it once per model, under a design only: *"Model: logistic regression; OR = odds ratio (…); t(18) on 20 design df."* The two numbers answer different questions — `t(18)` is what this model's intervals were referred to, `20 design df` is the design's own — so the design's df became a **table** fact in the model record (`reg_call(x)$design_degf`), which is where a fact no column can carry belongs.

**C2 — the two decisions were separated, not just fixed.** `reg_gap_se_of()` divided every printed half-width by z on the stated ground that "the gap test is a z test throughout", but the interval it reads was built with **t** on any gaussian, quasi or `svyglm` column, so the recovered SE came back inflated by exactly `qt(df)/z`. It recovers with the column's own `conf_level_to_crit(get_conf_level(col), get_degf(col))` now — which G7's stamp is what makes possible — and still TESTS with z, the convention `fmt_gap_bounds()` / `fmt_gap_p()` share and the only one open to the `adjustment` gap, whose SE is an influence-function sandwich referring to no df at all. `crit` and the now-dead `conf_level` left both signatures. Verified against `summary(lm)` on a gaussian `between_groups` table; the binomial case is byte-identical (z either way).

**C3 — `+ 0`.** `p$sign * pmax(0, |gap| - half)` is IEEE **negative zero** when the near bound is pinned and the score is negative, and `sprintf("%+.1f", -0)` prints `-0.0 pts` — which reads as "just excludes the null" beside a p-value saying the opposite. Per the maintainer's call the rendering changes and nothing else: no bare-neutral form, no cue. Only the additive branch ever showed it (`exp(-0)` is 1).

**Part 5 — the crude influence function READS its contrast instead of assuming one** (maintainer's call: fix the maths, not guard it). `reg_crude_if_maker()` builds the crude leg of every `color = "adjustment"` gap — it is load-bearing, not dead code — and hard-coded a category-**vs-rest** indicator while ignoring the pivot it was already handed. Vs-rest is right for a marginal probability contrast and wrong for a multinomial's own conditional odds ratio, which is vs-**pivot** and which xiii-1 made the interval compute. Both arms exist now, chosen from what the estimator already says (3+ categories AND a logit link ⇒ vs-pivot): the vs-pivot arm zeroes the weights outside the {category, pivot} pair, so `mu` becomes the share within the pair and the existing residual formula gives its log-odds unchanged. **Verified against hand values: 0.0705207 both ways on the restricted 2×2 (exactly Woolf), and the vs-rest arm still reproduces the hand risk-difference SE exactly** — so the reachable path is provably untouched. The latent arm ships tested even though no user-facing path reaches it yet.

**One smaller fix rode along**: `forest_plot()`'s gap band used `conf_level_to_z()`, which **rounds** to 1.96 (it exists to name colour BREAKS), while `fmt_gap_bounds()` uses the unrounded 1.959964 — the comment claimed machine precision and meant 2e-5. It uses `zscore_formula()` now.

**Tests**: five blocks, each pitched to fail before its fix and each guarded against going vacuous. `test-survey-crude.R` — the design refit IS `confint(svyglm)` (plus method / degf / `n_eff`, and a non-vacuous comparison against the closed form on the same grid), and a split-off twin asserting the weights rung KEEPS the closed form on its own effective base. `test-tab_reg-empirical.R` — the multinomial numeric row, against the univariable `multinom` (⚠ tolerance 1e-4: two independent `nnet::multinom` runs agree only to its optimiser's convergence). `test-tab_reg-survey.R` — every column of a fit shares one df across all three contrasts, the crude column's is strictly larger, the recovered SE equals `vcov(svyglm)`'s, and the footer names both numbers. `test-between-groups-gap.R` — the gaussian gap SE equals `summary(lm)`'s, and a hand-built pinned bound renders `+0.0 pts` (a fixture pins one only by luck, so the C3 test is a unit test). `test-adjustment-gap.R` — both influence-function arms against hand values, plus the binary case that needs no arm.

**Reported, not fixed**: a flat `svydesign(ids = ~1)` and a `wt =` table still give a crude column a different interval, because the flat design passes `svy_degf(design)` into the closed form where `wt =` passes `Inf`. Pre-existing (the `degf` argument has always been `design_spec$degf %||% Inf`), unrelated to this phase, and arguably right either way — but the two paths are meant to tell the same story, so it is a real inconsistency for whoever next touches the basis ladder.
