**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 9484**. `devtools::document()` clean; one export added (`shape_numeric_var`), one renamed (`tab_shape` -> `tab_structure`). 36 `_golden/*.rds` regenerated after `dev/verify_golden_field_delta.R` proved the delta over 1788 cells is ONE field's value and nothing else; `golden.md`'s 202 moved lines are all numeric-column lines, every colour class unchanged.

**One vocabulary, one file: `R/var-shape.R`.** `shape` was a regression argument living in `R/reg-assumptions.R`, which no crosstab may read. The producer-agnostic half moved out and became a declared table: `VAR_SHAPES`, one row per shape with its `kind`, what it `produces` (`factor` / `numeric` / `term`), its `producers`, its header `mark` and its user-facing `doc`. `REG_SHAPES` is gone — `shape_vocab(producer)` is the derived view, so the two producers cannot hold two lists, and **a refusal is derived rather than written**: `tab(shape = "quadratic")` says *a curvature is a model term, use `"quintiles"` to see the curve as groups*, read off the row. `?shape_numeric_var`'s whole value list is generated from the same `doc` column. Left behind in `reg-assumptions.R` is only what is genuinely about a FIT — the quadratic TERM and its formula injection, beside the Linearity check whose cure it is. Moved with it and renamed for what they are: `per_variable()` (the shared unnamed-is-a-fallback grammar, now carrying the caller's own noun so a crosstab says *variable* and a model says *predictor*), `shape_wquantile()`, and `wtd_mean()` / `wtd_sd()` to `utils.R` — a crosstab calling `reg_predictor_sd()` was the kind of trace this phase is for.

**`tab(shape =)` rides in `...`, and its docs are generated.** `TAB_ARGS$shape` gains `producers = c("tab","tab_reg")` and `dots = "tab"`, so `tab_dots_rd()` writes the `@param ...` paragraph and links `?shape_numeric_var`; `shape_name` (default `TRUE`) is a second such row. Nothing entered `tab()`'s signature and no list is hand-kept.

**RESOLVED in `tab_setup()`, APPLIED in `tab_prepare_pop()`, and the split is the design.** What a variable WILL be is an argument fact the col_var num/text classification must already know — a column about to be cut is a factor to the spine whatever its column still holds — so resolution happens before that block, and `"auto"` is decided there too (it needs the data, which is present). WHERE it is cut is a fact about the population, so the cutting waits until after the filter and the NA policy, and runs **once on the whole database, before the row_var loop and any `tab_vars` split** — the behaviour `tab_reg()` already had, and the only one under which sub-tables are comparable. From that line a shaped variable is an ordinary factor: the levels resolution, both leaves, the chi², the intervals and the colour engine needed no code at all. Two long-standing defects fall out: `fct_lump_min()` no longer aborts on a numeric row_var (it is a factor by then, and the `across()` is restricted to factors and excludes shaped columns, since lumping bands would undo the cut), and a numeric row variable at last gets `cleannames`, `levels_collapse` and the reserved-level check.

**The `"auto"` rule, and why not plain `sd_bands`.** The maintainer proposed `sd_bands` for every numeric row/tab variable; measured against real data that would band a 1-7 Likert item or a 0-5 count, where one row per value is exactly what is wanted. So: **few distinct WHOLE values (`tx_option("shape_auto_max")`, default 12) -> `"levels"`, otherwise `"sd_bands"`**, said in one message per call naming the override. `"levels"` is a `VAR_SHAPES` row of its own, so it can be asked for by name — and it returns a **plain, unprefixed** factor, deliberately: that is exactly what a numeric row variable has always become, so a table built this way stays identical to one built before `shape` existed **and to `tab_counts()`'s on the same keys**. ⚠ Both halves were measured: making it `ordered` broke three `counts-parity` assertions, and prefixing its first level with the variable's name broke the parity outright (`yr: 2000` against `2000`). The two real CUTS are ordered and prefixed, because their order and their "levels of what?" are facts they add.

**The labels.** `[18,30) low` / `[30,48) below average` / `[48,65) above average` / `[65,89] high` — the real cut points, then in words where the band sits, derived from the surviving landmarks so a skewed variable that lost one still names its bands right; `[18,33) Q1` for quantile groups; the variable's name on the FIRST level only (`age: [18,30) low`). Breaks on a whole-numbered variable are snapped UP to the whole number, which with `right = FALSE` is the **identical cut** (measured: the four band counts are unchanged) and turns `[29.89,47.18)` into `[30,48)`. The regression side takes the same labels — no back-compatibility is owed there, and `m-sd..m` was never readable.

**A transform renames its column.** `shape = c(age = "log")` gives `log_age`, because the mean of a logarithm is not the logarithm of a mean and a column headed `age` would state the wrong quantity — in the console, in the returned tibble and in every export alike, which is why it is a rename and not a display label. It happens at `tab()`'s variable boundary, where the roles are still just names. ⚠ The name must be **syntactic**: `log(age)` was tried and fails, because tab()'s pipeline reads its variable names back with `as.character()` over a list of symbols, which deparses, and a deparsed non-syntactic name returns wrapped in backticks — it stops matching its own column. `log`/`sqrt` are refused on the row and tab axes, where a number has no rows.

**`{sd}` and `{cv}`, and the end of a 45-line special case.** `format()` folded a mean's sd in by hand (`disp_mean_sd`), and two more sites re-derived `sqrt(var)` themselves. Both are now ordinary DERIVED tokens (`settable = FALSE`, like `resid` and `gap`), `mean_sd` = `"{mean} (σ{sd})"` and `mean_cv` = `"{mean} (cv {cv})"` are ordinary presets, and the generic composite path does the rest — **better**, since its per-token padding aligns the means themselves, which the hand-rolled tail never did. `mat_sd_twin()` went with it: 22c-ii's `mat_aside_cols()` already splits every aside into an Excel column, and the sd is now one of them. Two declared columns replaced what would have been branches: `unit = "pct"` (print ×100 with a `%`, so `format()` reads no hard-coded token list) and `self_named` (the CELL says "cv", so an export header drops that aside — `mean`, not `mean (cv)` — while the console tag keeps it).

**The default is `mean_cv`, GUARDED per column.** Research first: a coefficient of variation is unstable near a zero mean, meaningless on an interval scale, and negative when the mean is. `tab()` cannot know a column is ratio-scale, so `num_default_display()` reads the column's OWN means and chooses `mean_cv` only when every one is strictly positive, the bare mean otherwise. One layout per column — never a wild figure in some rows and a sensible one in others. (No symbol exists for a CV the way σ does for an sd; the word is three characters and self-naming, which the header rule then uses.)

**The reported `ordered` abort no longer reproduces — but it was masking two live defects, and a third.** 22c-i's `lvl_ptype2_union()` swallows the refusal, so the join now DEGRADES silently instead of aborting: measured, `tab(d, rincome, tvhours, tab_vars = race, totaltab = "table")` returned an unordered index with an `rbindlist` warning. (1) `num_total_postprocess()` called `fct_na_value_to_level()` **ungated** — the exact defect 22c-i fixed in `num_core()`'s main path, surviving in the total-rollup tail, and firing on the very column the two leaves are joined on. (2) `num_rollup()`'s own comment stated the ORDERED hazard and then applied its shared-ptype cure to `tab_vars` only, exempting the row_var; it now restates the source's levels for every index key, which is `plain_core()`'s `finalize_total_rows()` written on the other leaf. ⚠ Gating "Total" on `drop_keys` was tried and is wrong — a tab_var is a grouping key in one rollup of a series and a drop_key in the next, and the two are bound together. (3) `vec_ptype2.tabxplor_lvl.factor` returned the bare union, **dropping the row-index declaration** on any bind against an undeclared factor, after which the next ordered bind was unprotected again.

**One more, found by the new default.** A transposed render materialises as `"xl"` (it needs the `n` COLUMN), so `mat_aside_cols()` was splitting the aside off and the flipped cell lost it. It is gated on a genuine Excel render now: a transpose writes a formatted STRING for every backend, so the composite survives the flip whole.

**Verification and tests.** New `test-var-shape.R` (60 assertions): the vocabulary and its derived refusals, both cutters' breaks / balance / weighting / freezing, the degrade-not-abort on a skewed variable, the whole-number snap proved identical to the raw cut, the name-on-the-first-level rule and the `tab_counts()` parity it must not break, `shape_numeric_var()` equal to what `tab(shape =)` builds, the `"auto"` threshold and its message, the cut-once-per-table guarantee, the column rename, and the two derived tokens with the CV guard. `dev/verify_golden_field_delta.R` gained a `CHANGED_FIELDS` mode (a field whose VALUE may move, stated as a predicate) — the four previous modes could not express a layout change.

⚠ **Left open, on purpose**: the jamovi display ComboBoxes do not offer `mean_sd` / `mean_cv` and there is no `shape` control (Phase 22g's batched `prepare()`); the vignettes teach neither (Phase 23a owns numeric-variable teaching).


##### Phase 22c-iv — tooltips consistency and display presets

**DONE.** The hover layer was the one renderer that had never joined the declarative architecture: 15 hand-written fragments, each carrying its own gate, in an order written as a list literal — and `dev/tooltip_consistency_review.md` had measured 21 defects in it. It is now **one declared table and one builder**, in a file of its own (`R/tab-tooltip.R`, which takes ~190 lines out of `tab_classes.R`), under one sentence: *a tooltip is a rendering of the cell's own record — every value through `format()` on the column's own scale, every line named by the token it renders, one gate deciding them all.* Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 9503**; the goldens do not move at all and `_snaps/render-html.md` moves on exactly 12 tooltips, each gaining one fragment, with **zero non-tooltip diff lines**.

**`TOOLTIP_LINES` — a row per line, row order IS the reading order.** Each row states the `DISPLAY_TOKENS` key it renders (a foreign key checked at load), where its name comes from, which of the five shared gates apply, its optional column-level `when`, and its renderer where `format(set_display())` is not enough. The order is what the table teaches: **what this cell IS** (the estimate, with the interval and the exact p the cell cannot show) · **the level it sits on** · sd · **how far it sits from its reference** (diff · ratio · OR · std diff · ctr · resid) · **what it is compared to** (obs · gap) · **what it rests on** (n · note). `sd:` no longer opens every mean tooltip ahead of the deviation the table is about.

**One gate, stated once**: non-empty · comparable (not its own 100 % base) · not a reference cell · not already shown by the cell (`fmt_display_shows()`, over the whole template) · not already emitted by an earlier line. That single rule closes four findings at once — `OR: 1` on a reference cell, the `diff:` / `ratio:` that repeated a composite's own aside, the `ci:` that repeated the cell's own bracket one decimal wider, and the two lines that fired where the column had nothing to compare. Two of its clauses are keyed on the **quantity**, not the token: `diff` and `coef` are one number written two ways, `ci` and `moe` one interval, so a cell showing either suppresses both.

**The reference mask is role-aware, and the baseline row needs no plumbing.** `fmt_ref_cells()` (beside `get_reference()`, twin of `format()`'s own `ref_base()`) reads `is_refrow()` wherever `role` is non-empty and the crosstab rule otherwise — the tooltip was the last consumer still asking the crosstab question of a regression column, which is why a crude column printed `diff: 0% ; ratio: 1` on the very row its model twin marked `ref`. And since **a reference cell sits at the neutral value of its scale** — the rule `format()` already uses to print the bare `1` / `0` — the regression **baseline row**, which is `in_refrow` and is *not* at the neutral, tells itself apart for free: comparison lines drop there, `ref` is not printed (it is the reference for nothing), and the row's own value keeps its interval and p but **takes no name**, since an odds column holds the baseline ODDS there and "OR" would be a lie. Measured before: `ref ; OR: 1/1.5 ; n: 13 015`, wrong twice over.

**The labels are the token tags, and they are not translated.** `DISPLAY_TOKENS$label` — built by 22c-ii for the export unit row and the console type tag — is now the hover's vocabulary too, so one word names a quantity everywhere it appears: `diff` / `ratio` / `OR` / `ctr` / `resid` / `obs` / `gap` / `n`, and the level line that used to open unlabelled is named by the token itself (`row%` / `col%` / `adj%` / `obs%`, through `reg_role_qualifier()`). `mean_ctr`, a code identifier printed to readers, is gone; `obs:` and `crude:`, two names for one thing, are one. **Every `gettext()` in the tooltip path is deleted** (maintainer's call): like the pillar type abbreviations, the tags stay the `fmt` FIELD names, so the hover teaches the fields a user reads with `$` and `mutate()` — and the collision that had `diff` and `gap` both printing *écart*, the package's own umbrella word for a deviation, disappears rather than being arbitrated. The msgids they leave behind (`diff`, `std diff`, `mean_ctr`, `contrib`, `std. residual`, `ref. group`, `gap`, `ref`) are Phase 23f's catalogue sweep; ⚠ `gettext("obs")` stays, shared with `reg_role_qualifier()`, which names a HEADER.

**Three names a bare field does not identify, each gated by a declared fact.** On a total row the `ctr` field holds the column's MEAN contribution — the divisor every cell is graded against, printed nowhere else — so it reads **`mean ctr`**, and drops entirely under `color_signif = "guaranteed_effect"`, where the measure becomes the standardized residual and that mean plays no part. Under a measure whose declared `ref_kind` is `"group"` (`color = "between_groups"`) `obs` holds the first group's estimate, so it reads **`ref grp`**. And the `sd` line is now an ordinary `{sd}` token (22c-iii), not a `var` column carrying a square root.

**T1/T2 are fixed in `format()`, so print, Markdown, Excel and the hover are corrected together.** The percentage mask asked *"is this column a mean?"* where it means *"is the quantity this token renders a percentage?"*, and `raw_diff` / `log_coef` declare `var_kind = "coef"` — so a gaussian beta of -3.6 printed **-364.1 %**, with a *correct* interval beside it. The condition is now `var_kind == "pct"`, checked against all 13 `EST_SCALES` rows: exactly the two coefficient scales move, and the derived risk difference of an odds-ratio column keeps its `%` (which is why `is_pct`, TRUE on three scales only, is the wrong fact here). The decimals floor follows the same split. Verified: **no golden moves** (no golden case builds a `tab_reg()` table) and the Excel numFmt parity tests stay green.

**The exact p-value now joins every estimate line** — it used to reach multiplicative columns only, because the branch that carried it was written for the hole the folded-CI line already covered. ⚠ It is gated on the column carrying no chi-squared contribution: `chi2_write_contrib()` OVERWRITES `pvalue` with the residual's, so where a table computed contributions the p belongs to the `resid` line and nowhere else.

**The odds ratio is shown on every `pct = "row"` / `"col"` column** (maintainer's call): it is computed on every one of them and used to appear only where the table was coloured by it. It obeys the shared gates, so a reference cell and 22c-ii's degenerate margin drop it by construction, plus one guard of its own — **never on the column the odds ratio takes as its baseline** (a whole column of 1s: under `pct = "row"` the first column IS the complementary category). ⚠ **The one thing to watch**: that baseline is the *first column*, not the reference column, so a cell can read `ratio: ×1.00 ; OR: 2.34` — both true, of two different 2×2s. The legend says which when the table is coloured by it; the hover does not, and a phrase long enough to say so is more than a hover line can hold.

**The two regression fragments go through `format()`.** The multinomial crude companion was a `sprintf()` of percentage POINTS beside a cell whose own bracket shows the crude ODDS RATIO — two estimands, three characters apart, neither saying which. It is now the observed **level and its interval**, built as an ordinary `fmt` cell and named `obs%` by the same token label as everything else (`tip_crude_level()`); the points difference is dropped as the third estimand it was. The numeric predictor's descriptive keeps its content and takes the hover's own words (`age: mean 47.2 (sd 17.4) ; yes 45.8 / no 49`).

**Two defects found on the way, both fixed.** (1) A **footer p-value row** came out as an estimate line with an empty value — `OR: , p = <0.01%` on the LR-vs-null row — because the old suppression tested the display TOKEN (`gof` / `blank`) and a p-value row displays `pvalue`; the builder now reads the ROW KIND as well. (2) `fmt_blank_fields()` cleared `diff` / `ci` / `mean` / `ctr` / `var` on a helper column but **kept `ratio` and `or`**, against its own comment, so a transposed table's base-count row hovered `ratio: ×1.00` over a count. Both fields are blanked now, and the `ref` word is restricted to **data rows**, which is what a synthetic base-count row is not.

**And one line stops repeating what the reader can already see**: `n:` is suppressed where a base-count column prints that row's count beside the cell (`tab_base_n_cols()` — every `tab_reg()` table, every spread). The html engine reads it once per table (`tab_base_n_values()`) and passes it like `.note`. ⚠ One gate to reverse if it proves wrong.

**Deliberately not done.** *T11, the weighted base* (maintainer's call): on a weighted table `n:` is still the unweighted count beside a weighted percentage — a zero-cost variant exists (render the base line's token as `wn` where the two differ). *T21, `+0` beside `-0.3`*: `print_num()` collapses a zero to `"0"` at any digit count, and the only non-ad-hoc fix — keeping the decimals — would make every reference cell print `0.0` / `0.0%` instead of the clean neutral the whole table is read against.

**Verification.** The full suite, alone. Beyond it, the seven captures of the review were re-run and read by hand (the gaussian coefficient, the crude column's reference row, the Constant row, the padded `Model_OR` bracket, the multinomial crude line, a row-% crosstab for the new OR line, `ci = "cell"`), plus the transposed render, whose tooltips are built per column and flipped. `tests/testthat/test-tooltips-14b.R` becomes **`test-tooltips.R`**, rewritten to the new vocabulary and gates and carrying six new blocks: the coefficient's missing `%`, the crude/model agreement on a reference row, the baseline row, the OR line and its baseline column, the un-repeated interval, and `mean ctr` under both significance policies. Four other files lose the old builder's name; `dev/tooltip_consistency_review.md` keeps its findings and gains a status line.

##### Phase 22c-v — one measure vocabulary, one alias table

⚠ **Read `dev/reg_estimand_api_redesign_follow_up.md` §7 before planning** — it holds the measured acceptance matrix, the four defects and the decision register (I4–I10). Decided there, do not re-derive: the acronyms stay permanent aliases and the **concept word stays what is taught**; there is no rename to `deviation` (§6, decisions I1/I2).

The measure vocabulary is declared **four times** (`COLOR_ALIASES` · `REG_MEASURE_ALIASES` + `REG_LOG_BASE` · `REG_LINK_ALIASES` · `DISPLAY_TOKENS$alias`) with four different coverages, so `tab(color = "rr")` aborts while `tab_reg(measure = "rr")` builds, and `tab(color = "IRR")` / `"RoM"` are refused although the regression side has taken them since 22a-iii. One declared acronym table beside `MEASURES` (`MEASURE_ACRONYMS`, with the all-lowercase twin **derived** rather than listed), read by two thin scoped views: the colour side adds the three legacy policy spellings, the regression side adds `cumOR`, the `log*` family and `auto`. `REG_LINK_ALIASES` stays separate — on `link` the word `log` means the log LINK, on `measure` it means "un-exponentiated". `DISPLAY_TOKENS` is **not** touched: an acronym names a measure, never a display token (I10). ⚠ One narrow exception landed in 22c-ii and does not reopen I10: `OR` is an alias ROW of the token `or`, because `or` is the one token whose canonical name is itself an acronym — a case-and-spelling tolerance on an existing token, not a fifth vocabulary. `or_pct` / `OR_pct` moved the other way, out of `DISPLAY_TOKENS` and into `DISPLAY_PRESETS` as alias presets of `or_base`.

Three deletions ride with it, all on the regression side, where no back-compatibility is owed: `reg_measure_key()`'s `tolower()` fallback (so `Difference` / `ODDS_RATIO` / `Rom` stop being legal — I5), and `risk_ratio` / `rate_ratio` (the taught long form is the concept word — I7). Two foreign keys replace the one that exists: every `REG_WORDS` acronym resolves through the shared table, and every `MEASURES` name is reachable from every argument its own `producers` column allows — which turns today's hand-written `tab()` / `tab_reg()` scope refusals into derived messages.

⚠ **And `fmt()` must validate `color` at last** (I9): measured, `fmt(n = 1L, color = "banana")` and `fmt(n = 1L, color = "IRR")` both store the string verbatim and the column then silently colours **nothing**, although `CLAUDE.md` describes the chain as *"`fmt()` (public, validates)"*. Both producers already normalise at their boundary, so `fmt()` is the last un-normalised writer; once it resolves through the shared table every stored `color` attribute is canonical. `measure_key()`'s `WARNING: on the hot path […] keep it a lookup` should be restated for what it really guards — measured, it costs 4.7 µs and runs 85 times building a 324-cell table, 55 on print, 129 in `tab_html()`, i.e. per (column × channel × backend), never per cell.

Nothing here changes a printed table, so no golden should move; `?tab`'s `@param color` and `?tab_reg`'s `@param measure` / `@param link` gain the completed alias list, and one `jmvtools::prepare()` is **not** needed (the jamovi pickers offer canonical names only).

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 9534**. `dev/verify_color_attrs.R` prints **IDENTICAL** over its 293 tables --- every stored colour attribute and every resolved slot vector unchanged. `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, three man pages rewritten. **No golden and no snapshot moved**, which is the phase's own gate: nothing here changes a printed table.

**One table, two scoped views, and the union is the header vocabulary.** `MEASURE_ACRONYMS` (`RD` / `diff` / `RR` / `IRR` / `RoM` / `OR`) sits beside `MEASURES`, with `MEASURE_ACRONYMS_REG` (`cumOR` / `D` / `WR`) declared next to it --- so a crosstab can refuse those three **by name** ("a `tab_reg()` spelling of `odds_ratio`") instead of calling them unknown, which matters because the header prints `Model_cumOR` and a reader will type it. The all-lowercase twin of each is **derived** (`measure_twins()`), with one declared clause: **a one-letter acronym gets none** --- `d` is a slip, not a spelling, and `REG_MEASURE_ALIASES` never had it. The two views are precomputed named vectors, `MEASURE_COLOR_KEYS` and `REG_MEASURE_SPELLINGS`, so `measure_key()` stays the pure lookup its hot path needs. ⚠ Read with a single `[`: on a named CHARACTER vector `[[` throws on a missing name, which would have turned every unknown spelling into an opaque subscript error at 200+ call sites.

**The maintainer's rule for the split, and it is derived rather than written.** *A word only a **rank** level names is one a crosstab can never print* --- a crosstab cell is a share, a mean or a count, while a rank is a share of PAIRS. `reg_model_only_words()` states it where the level kinds live, and two foreign keys hold `MEASURE_ACRONYMS_REG` to it, so a future family that adds a rank word cannot forget to scope it. Register **I8** is restated accordingly in `dev/reg_estimand_api_redesign_follow_up.md`: it said `cumOR` alone, having been written before 22c-vi existed, and its §7.3 code block would have invited a later reader to "restore" `D` / `WR` to the shared table.

**Eleven new foreign keys, three retargeted, and the two composed ones are the point.** `tx_fk()` compares value SETS one direction at a time, so the *(acronym → measure)* agreement is encoded as `"OR->odds_ratio"` strings (the `tx_fk_emp_shape_keys()` idiom) and checked **both ways**: every estimand the library composes has a typeable acronym, and every acronym names a measure some header prints. So `MEASURE_ACRONYMS` is **declared, not derived**, although it inverts exactly out of `REG_LEVEL_MEASURES` + `REG_FAMILIES$ordinal$words` --- deriving it would invert the file dependency (the colour engine's lookup existing only because `tab_reg()`'s header vocabulary does, across thirteen files of collation order) and, worse, would turn a build failure into a **silent** change of which strings `tab(color =)` accepts. ⚠ None of the new edges is `orphan = TRUE`: the orphan bucket is keyed by target signature, so an orphan edge onto `names(MEASURES)` would report `contrib` / `adjustment` / `between_groups` as dead weight and fail `test-fact-keys.R`.

**`REG_FIT_SPELLINGS` is derived, not listed.** Inverting `REG_FAMILIES$fits` on `REG_FIT_ONLY_FAMILIES` gives `rr → ratio`, `rd → difference`, `mr → ratio` --- so what `reg_formulas()` prints in its `fit` column can be typed straight back into `link`, and a new internal fit key needs no second declaration. ⚠ `reg_link_key()` consults `REG_LINK_ALIASES` **first**, and that order is load-bearing: `log` is the one word the two arguments do not share (the log LINK here, *un-exponentiated* on `measure`).

**`producers` could not answer the question the scope refusals ask, so `MEASURES` gained `color_arg`.** `producers` says who can BUILD a measure; `tab_reg()` builds `difference` / `ratio` / `odds_ratio` --- its columns are coloured on them --- yet its `color` argument names none of them, because there the estimand is `measure`'s job. Written as a two-armed `switch` the helper would have relocated the rule rather than unified it; as one declared scalar column it makes `measure_nameable(producer, channel =)` a pure filter, read by **all three** sites that stated the rule separately: `measure_validate()`, `reg_normalize_color()` and the generated `@param`. The refusal wording follows: the producer's own function name comes from `MEASURE_PRODUCER_FN` instead of a hardcoded `tab` / `tab_reg`, and the *"Valid measures"* hint now lists each measure with the acronyms that reach it --- the near-miss user is shown the word they actually typed. ⚠ `color_measures_rd()`'s `"text" %in% channels` filter was a latent no-op (all six rows carry `text`) and is carried as the helper's `channel =` argument rather than silently dropped.

**`fmt()` validates at last** (I9), by routing `color` through `resolve_color_channels()` --- the storage boundary `set_color()` already used --- and `color_signif` through `resolve_color_signif()`, split out of `set_color_signif()` for the purpose (a constructor has no `x` to set an attribute on). So **every writer of the `color` attribute now normalises**, and the maintainer's invariant holds by construction: *a stored `color` is always a canonical `MEASURES` key, never an acronym*, which is what makes it easy to program against. Two decisions written down at the site: `fmt()` normalises **without decoding** --- a legacy `"after_ci"` keeps its measure half and drops the policy half, exactly as `set_color()` does, so `tab()`'s boundary remains the one decoder; and validation must **never** move into `new_fmt()`, because `fmt_ptype_empty <- new_fmt()` runs at source time some 1900 lines before `MEASURES` is bound, which would fail the install outright.

**One test had to change, and it was the only one in the suite.** `test-fmt_class.R`'s 16-attribute merge fixture built `fmt(color = c("contrib", "OR"))`; `OR` now normalises to `odds_ratio`, which is text-only, so the background-channel refusal fires --- the pair is `c("ratio", "difference")` now, which keeps the block's non-vacuity guard against the other fixture's `c("diff", "ratio")`. Otherwise: the acceptance matrix's new positives and the three scoped negatives in `test-color-config.R` (plus the canonical-storage invariant and `measure_nameable()`), and in `test-reg-estimand.R` the fit-key round trip and negatives for `Difference` / `DIFF` / `MR` / `risk_ratio` / `d` --- I5 and I7 were otherwise asserted by nothing at all.

**Also landed:** the jamovi `measure` picker named two words that are no longer header acronyms (`MR`, `AME`); its labels read `ratio (RR / IRR / RoM)` and `difference (RD / diff)`. No option name, value or default changed, so nothing goes inert; and the generated JS does not carry picker titles (verified --- the suite's JS-drift test is green), so no `dev/generate_jamovi_js.R` re-run either. The two labels reach a running module with **22g's batched `jmvtools::prepare()`**.

⚠ **Left open, and reported rather than fixed**: `reg-resolve.R`'s `!is.na(color_arg[1])` guard means `color = c(TRUE, "adjustment")` skips the storage-boundary pair check entirely (pre-existing, harmless today because the second slot is validated on its own) --- for whichever phase revisits that boundary.

##### Phase 22c-vi — one last tab_reg() feature: "ordinal" one column marginal effects

**DONE.** `family = "ordinal"` now reports on the **order, in one column**, in a probability a non-statistician can read. `measure = "difference"` gives Somers' **`D`** (`win - loss = 2γ - 1`), `measure = "ratio"` the **win ratio** (`win / loss`), and `{base}` is **γ, the probability of superiority** — *of two people, one from this group and one from the reference group, how often does the one from this group end up higher on the scale, a tie counting half*. `measure = "odds_ratio"` at `effect = "conditional"` is unchanged (`cumOR`, still the default). The design and every measurement behind it are in `dev/ordinal_one_column_effects.md`.

**What was removed, and why it is not a loss.** The K-column ordinal route is gone: `REG_FAMILIES$ordinal$level` went `"pct"` → `"rank"`, so the library composes 5 rows instead of 10 (conditional `cumOR` + its log; marginal `D`, `WR` + its log). Measured on `gss_simple`, the four marginal-RR columns were one parameter refracted four ways — the per-*level* risk differences sum to exactly 0 (2.8e-17), and the ordinal columns come out monotone **by construction** (`×1.17 ×1.11 ×1.06 ÷1.09` for Black) while an unconstrained multinomial on the same data shows the real, non-monotone pattern with the first cut not significant (`×1.07 ×1.18** ×1.19*** ÷1.12***`) — and Brant rejects proportional odds here (χ² = 65.2, df = 28, p = 8.5e-05). So `family = "multinomial"` is now the answer to "I want per-category numbers", and it is the better one whenever proportional odds is in doubt. The three now-unreachable `REG_EMPIRICAL$ordinal` per-category shapes were deleted with it.

**Why this measure and not another.** Three measured facts, each of which decided a design choice: (1) at **K = 2** the pair collapses onto the binomial family's own measures — `win - loss` IS the risk difference to machine precision, `win / loss` IS the odds ratio — so ordinal became the exact continuation of binomial rather than a new concept; (2) it is **collapsible** — with a covariate independent of the exposure (no confounding to find) the cumulative OR moves 1.47 → 2.24 while the marginal pair does not move at all, which is what turns `color = "adjustment"` from a description into a **test** here, and it is why the *marginal* (unmatched) definition was taken over Agresti & Kateri's matched one, which does drift (+0.024); (3) it **survives PO violation** — γ from `polr` and from `multinom` agree to ≤0.0033 on data where Brant rejects. `D` leads the level's measure list (so `auto` picks it) because it is stable in K where the win ratio drifts (0.212 → 0.227 vs 1.79 → 1.63, K = 4 → 20).

**Almost all of it is declaration.** One `REG_LEVEL_MEASURES$rank` entry (`difference → points/D`, `ratio → pct_ratio/WR`, `odds_ratio → odds_ratio/OR`) — **no new `EST_SCALES` row, no new `COLOR_SCALES` ladder, no new `fmt` field, no new `var_kind`**: `points` and `pct_ratio` already declare exactly the right geometry, and measured, the package's own ×1.1/×1.2/×1.5/×2 rungs map to `D` = 0.030/0.057/0.126/0.212, near-invariant in K — `pct_diff`'s declared anchor is already *"5 points at a 50 % reference"*, which is literally what `D` measures. Two `REG_WORDS` rows (`D`, `WR`, both `noncollapsible = FALSE`) plus their `REG_MEASURE_ALIASES` twins; one clause in `reg_compose_row()` refusing `at_reference` on a rank (a pair drawn at one profile is the matched, non-collapsible estimand); and rank arms in the three prose sites that key on the level kind. ⚠ **A level kind is no longer a `var_kind`** — stated once in `reg-estimand.R`'s header and in the `REG_FAMILIES$level` gloss; deliberately no fourth `var_kind`, since five places answer "percentage" for an unknown one instead of erroring.

**Two ad-hoc predicates became declared facts.** `reg_fam_percategory()` (a family-name test that decided the column count) is deleted: the row now carries a derived **`per_level`**, so "how many columns this estimand needs" lives where every other column-shape fact already did (`REG_EMPIRICAL$*$per_category`). What is left of the old predicate is renamed `reg_fam_3plus()` and asked only what it really tests — "fitted by multinom/polr". Likewise `reg_crude_saturated()` no longer names `"ordinal"`: the shape declares **`refit`**, which only `cumor`/`cumor_log` do (proportional odds is a constraint, so a one-factor polr is not the cell table), and the rank shapes take the closed form.

**One estimator, two callers.** `reg_rank_pair()` is the whole arithmetic — two distributions in, both readings plus the gradient in each distribution out — and it runs on the model column's two **standardised** distributions and on its crude twin's two **counted** ones. That identity is the point: one formula, two inputs, so the distance between the columns means adjustment and nothing else. The pairwise double sum over people factorises exactly into the two column means (verified against brute force), so `reg_gcomp_rank_maker()` is O(K) post-processing of numbers the sweep already forms — and, answering once, it is a **drop-in for `reg_gcomp_maker()`**: `reg_marginal_gcomp()`, `reg_marginal_column()`, `reg_wald_finalize()` and `reg_delta_se()` needed no arm. At `est = γ` the gradient IS DeLong's placement value, so the crude variance is arrived at rather than special-cased. `reg_ame_if_maker()` gained a `g =` parameter instead of a third near-identical copy.

**Verified numerically, not by inspection:** the analytic jacobian matches numeric differentiation to 3e-10 on both links; the crude closed-form SE matches a 3 000-draw multinomial bootstrap (0.01326 vs 0.01351); the **gap SE** matches a 200-draw paired bootstrap (0.004111 vs 0.004075). All three are pinned in `tests/testthat/test-reg-rank.R` (10 tests), along with the K = 2 reduction and the collapsibility simulation.

**Three things the phase gained on the way.** (1) A 3+ level outcome finally has a real **observed column with an interval** — `Obs_D`, a closed form on the outcome × predictor table, where before its crude value could only ride in the model cell as a point; `reg_emp_mode()` returns `"column"` for it with no special-casing, because the new shapes are not `per_category`. (2) A **numeric** predictor's crude cell was silently blank on this route: `reg_empirical_fit()` was asking its sweep for a per-category AME. It now threads the contrast, and `age` reads `+10.7%***` crude against `+8.1%***` adjusted. (3) **Weighted ordinal marginals now work at all** — `reg_prob_engine()` accepts `svyolr` (⚠ NOT a `polr` subclass, and its `coef()` carries the thresholds too, so the split is by class and by name, never by length — a length rule silently truncates plain `polr`), its `vcov()` is already design-based so `reg_delta_se()` needed no branch, and survey clause J exempts rank estimands. Verified on flat weights and on a stratified design. Only the gap test is unavailable there (no per-observation scores), so `color = "adjustment"` colours without testing under a design.

**The Constant row is void on a rank column, and the footer names the scale.** A model's predicted outcome distribution is a fact about the outcome, not the level these effects move away from — that one is a coin flip, and the reference row already prints it. A 50 % Constant cell would restate the row above it with a number that can never move. Instead `reg_outcome_scale()` stores the ordered levels and their shares and the footer prints `rincome, from low to high: 1-Lt $10000 (17%) < ... < 4-$25000 or more (57%)` — necessary, because a one-column table shows the outcome's name and none of its categories.

**Docs:** `?tab_reg`'s estimand grid and acronym table regenerate from the tables; `vignettes/tabxplor-reg.Rmd` gained the one-column teaching in *Ordinal and nominal outcomes* and a tested crude/adjusted pair in *An ordered outcome*, and lost two claims that stopped being true (a 3+ level outcome having no observed column; a weighted ordinal model having no marginal quantities). The Brant bullet now names both cures. `dev/generate_jamovi_js.R` was re-run — no new jamovi option, so **no `jmvtools::prepare()` is needed for this phase**.

⚠ **Open, for the phase that owns it:** `vignettes/tabxplor-reg-fr.Rmd`'s ordinal section is now stale, for **23f**. (`D` / `WR` joined the unified alias table in **22c-v**, scoped regression-only.)








#### Phase 22d — Black and white publication print manual review

##### Phase 22d-i — formatting change

```r
options(tabxplor.theme = "print", tabxplor.print = "html", tabxplor.cleannames = TRUE)
tab(gss_simple, c(race, relig), c(party3, tvhours), pct = "row", na = "drop_all", 
   color = "difference", color_signif = "grey_non_signif",
)
```

- bold only applies to the primary display token (right behaviour), but underline and italics also apply to the secondary display tokens: they too, like colors, should only apply to the primary display token by default (global option). Otherwise it’s noise.
- bold is more visually striking than underline, and italics is subtle and not striking (specially with the current html monospace font).
I want to try something a bit different (then, I’ll decide with visual review):
1. `tx_chrome_hex("print")$grey` identifies the greyed-out cells (the "#888888" grey is much lighter than with colors)
2. the direction information is carried by : "over" have underline ; "under" have italics and no underline
3. the size of effect is carried by a 3 rungs ladder: "#333333" text ; "#000000" text ; "#000000" + bold text.

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 7840**. `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**, five man pages with prose-only edits. The 36 `_golden/*.rds` did not move at all; `_snaps/golden.md` moved by exactly **9 CSS rules x 16 tables, every one of them inside the `@media print` layer** (plus 22b-v's two pending `.tx-spark` rules, accepted with it).

**The two axes are split, and that is the whole change.** DIRECTION is now the face alone -- over is UNDERLINED, under is ITALIC and never underlined -- and MAGNITUDE is an ink ladder the palette gained: `#333333`, then `#000000`, then `#000000` + **bold**. Bold is the loudest signal a page has, so it now marks the strongest deviation instead of a mere direction, and italic (the quietest, especially in the html monospace font) no longer has to compete with it. Three rungs over four break slots, mapped **1 | 2 | 3-4** per the maintainer's call: `legend_break_tokens()`'s existing "drop a break that renders like the previous one" rule then collapses slots 3 and 4 for free, so the print legend reads `+5 ; +10 ; +20` where the colour legend lists four thresholds. Nothing was added to make that work -- the collapse rule already keyed on the full (hex, bold, italic, underline) tuple.

**The greyed-out cell is deliberately light, and the test now says so.** The maintainer's `tx_chrome_hex("print")` tweak (`grey` `#595959` -> `#888888`, `grey2` `#111111` -> `#333333`) broke two WCAG assertions **on purpose**: greyed means "harder to read on purpose", so it is held to the large-text / non-text floor (3:1 on white, measured 3.54) and merely to VISIBLE on the deepest fill (1.79), never to the 4.5:1 body-text floor a cell meant to be read must meet. Both are restated in those terms with the reason in the comment, and one is ADDED that the old pair never made: the reading ladder itself must be monotone -- greyed lighter than rung 1 lighter than rung 2 (L* 56.7 / 21.2 / 0; bold rides rung 2, so the last step is typographic rather than a third shade). `tx_chrome_hex()`'s comment argued for `#595959` at 3.53:1 and is rewritten. `grey2` gains a THIRD reader on the way -- the aside's ink, an uncoloured cell in an uncoloured column, and the ladder's first rung are one hex, all three meaning "present, set slightly back".

**The face stops at the primary token, like the colour.** Two paths carried it to a cell and both had to move. (1) The slot class sits on the `<td>`, so `.p1{text-decoration:underline}` underlined the aside too -- `.tabxplor-tab .tx-sec` now carries three print-only declarations. WARNING recorded at the site: **`display:inline-block` is the load-bearing one, not `text-decoration:none`** -- a CSS text-decoration is drawn by the ancestor box across everything inside it and CANNOT be switched off by a descendant; only an atomic inline box is left out of it. (2) The `<b>/<i>/<u>` markup wrapped the whole cell; it is applied inside `html_cell_text()` now, to the primary piece only, and the engine's separate `html_face_wrap()` call is kept solely for the two whole-cell cases (`color_whole_cell`, and a degraded column carrying no face flags). `html_face_wrap()`'s own signature is untouched -- it is locked by `test-19m-defects.R`. Measured on a coloured composite cell: `<td class="... p1"><u>24%</u><span class="tx-sec"> (1 305)</span></td>`, and under the opt-out `<td class="... p1"><u>24%<span class="tx-sec"> (1 305)</span></u></td>`.

**One switch, widened rather than duplicated** (maintainer's call): `options(tabxplor.color_whole_cell = TRUE)` now opts out of the whole primary/secondary split -- colour and face alike. A second option would have been a second rule to remember for one idea; `?tabxplor-options` says "the cell's rendering" where it said "the colour".

**The legend names the direction, not the loudest face.** `legend_shade_names()`'s print pair is `Underlined` / `Italic` (the ink ramp is the magnitude, which the coloured break-words already show). One msgid moved: `po/R-fr.po` + `po/R-tabxplor.pot` + the compiled `inst/po/fr/LC_MESSAGES/R-tabxplor.mo`, verified rendering *"Souligne : cases >= a la ligne Total +5 ; +10 ; +20 points. Italique : ..."*. The 9 fuzzy / 106 untranslated msgids are pre-existing debt for Phase 23f.

**One test defect found and fixed, and it was a real trap.** `test-tab_md.R`'s pandoc-validity check looked for the bare word `"line-block"` in the rendered html as its "pandoc refused this table" marker -- but `h` carries our inlined stylesheet, where it is a substring of **`display:inline-block`**. Six cases failed while every table rendered perfectly. The marker is pandoc's own element now (`class="line-block"`), with the reason at the site.

**Accepted losses, both documented rather than worked around.** `tab_plot()` maps the face onto ggplot2's `fontface`, which has no underline, so an over-represented cell is told apart by its INK alone there (the plot backends are frozen legacy; `forest_plot` is Phase 22f). And Markdown and Excel colour a cell as a whole, so their face follows their colour -- the aside keeps it in those two media, exactly as it keeps the colour.

**Unchanged, deliberately:** the background channel (one grey fill ramp, magnitude only -- a fill cannot carry a direction), `bg_legend` (the font stand-in where a fill is impossible), `fmt_point_palette()`'s print deviation for plotted marks, and `set_color_palette()`'s provable inability to touch the print palette.

##### Phase 22d-ii — new print palettes

I want 3 black and white typo text palettes (plus only one background greys palette, the current one).

1. The current palette, with less effect size breaks (only 3) but working everywhere.

2. Regression first palette, to use mostly with `tab_reg()`, where the direction is already given by a clear symbol in every cell (`+`|`-` `×`|`÷` `x`|`1/x` depending on the `measure`) :
- Italics for the "below null"/"under" branch, subtle but which only have to support the over|under symbols
- The size of effect is carried by a 4 rungs ladder: "black" text ; "black" + bold text ; "black" + bold + underline ; "black" + bold + double underline.
- A possibility to use it with `tab()` pct and means is `display = "{base} ({ratio})"`, so that ratio `×`|`÷` symbols carries the direction the same way.

3. Repeated superscript marks, to use with no stars, rather used in `tab()` than in `tab_reg()` (where stars are default)
- The direction is carried by `+` or `-`.
- The size of effect is carried by a 4 rungs ladder of repeated superscript marks in both directions: `+` `++` `+++` `++++` `-` `--` `---` `----`, at the same positon than current stars, everything padded and aligned for human readability like everytime.
- Look at the original idea in `dev/black_and_white_publication_palette.md`.
- Please study how superscripts do in the current monospace fonts, in html, in Excel, etc. Would there be a possibility to only use 2 base characters length for them, replacing blanks with half-character lenghts, and still ensuring alignement (to avoid wasting around 4 horizontal spaces per column) ? I guess in markdown only the symbols without superscript would be better (superscript would waste horizontal space in the raw unrendered markdown) ?

In all scenarios, `tx_chrome_hex("print")$grey` identifies the greyed-out cells.
- Currently the grey is much lighter than with colors ("#aaaaaa"), because it’s needed for the first palette to have 3 visually striking rungs on the luminance scale: please calculate it’s oklch contrast and tell me if it’s acceptable and good practice for a greyed-out cell on pure white background ; if not acceptable, the only solution is to only have 2 rungs for effect size in the first palette.
- Print palettes 2 and 3 would not need such a light grey since they won’t use a darker grey as rung 1: would there be a reliable and integrated way to change the framework to allow different "greyed-out" colors for different palettes, without adding white elephants ? Then, we could go back to "#888888" for grey-out cells in print palettes 2 and 3.

There should be a user-friendly way to decide which palette to use, global options + override possibility in `tab_export()`. Each should have a readable and easily understandable name. Also, the current code of the print palette is not easily modifiable by me, because not every formatting are at the same place, would there be a way to make it more readable for humans, visually seeing what typos and chromes define a color break at the same place ?

**DONE.** Suite **FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 4 | PASS 7932** -- and that closes the **20 failures that were pre-existing at HEAD** when the phase started (16 `golden display` snapshots carrying 22d-i's un-accepted CSS diff, and 4 `test-print-palette.R` contrast/ink assertions against the hand-edited greys): nothing is left red. `devtools::document()` clean, **NAMESPACE unchanged**; 11 man pages rewritten, all with identical `\usage` and `\item{}` name sets except `?format.tabxplor_fmt`, which gains the one new formal. The 36 `_golden/*.rds` did **not** move; `_snaps/golden.md` moved by exactly **3 CSS declarations x 16 tables, every one inside the `@media print` layer** (the pending 22d-i diff plus this phase's grey), and `_snaps/golden.new.md` -- a failing-snapshot artifact committed by mistake in `637ea9d` -- is deleted.

**The grid IS the definition, and that is the phase's real deliverable.** A print palette was three unrelated literals -- an ink ramp in `default_print_palette()`, three parallel 8-logical vectors in `tx_palette_faces()`, and a grey buried in `tx_chrome_hex()`'s `switch` two files away -- so "what does break 2 look like" could not be read anywhere. It is now one row of one `tribble` per break slot, carrying its ink, weight, slant, rule and mark side by side, in **`R/tab-palettes.R`**, beside every other palette. `default_print_palette()` and `tx_palette_faces()` are both **deleted** -- the first because the grid replaces it, the second because after the merge its only unique content was the colour palettes' one constant fact, and `build_palettes()` now assembles ink, face and ANSI style the same way for every palette: light, dark, then a loop over `PRINT_PALETTES`. The face record's SHAPE is written ONCE (`face_record()`), so a constant face and a graded one are the same object built two ways rather than two hand-rolled literals. A fourth publication palette is one row in the table and reaches every backend, the stylesheet and the legend with no other edit. The one principle the file states, because every palette is a choice of how to apply it: **an ordered channel (ink, emphasis, a repeated mark) carries MAGNITUDE; a selective channel (underline vs italic, or the cell's own +/- symbol) carries DIRECTION.**

**Three palettes, selected by `theme` -- no new argument anywhere.** `"print"` (`"bw"` still its alias) keeps 22d-i's design unchanged; `"print_emphasis"` spends everything on magnitude -- pure black ink, bold, then a rule, then a DOUBLED rule -- for a table whose cells already carry their direction (`tab_reg()`'s own `+`/`-`, `x`/`div`, `x`/`1/x` glyphs, or `tab()` under `display = "{base} ({ratio})"`), with italic left as the quiet second voice under the null; `"print_marks"` says it all in characters. `tx_resolve_theme()` reads its value list from `names(PRINT_PALETTES)`, and every hard-coded `identical(theme, "print")` became `tx_is_print()` -- one predicate, seven sites. `tab_css()` carries exactly one publication palette: the one the page is rendered in, or the one a COLOURED page falls back to on paper, which is `print_rules` -- widened from a logical to `TRUE` / `FALSE` / a palette name, no signature change. `"print_marks"` is refused there with the reason: its marks are cell text, and a media query can restyle a page but cannot add characters to it.

**The greyed-out cell is a per-PALETTE fact now, and the maintainer's question has a number.** `#aaaaaa` measures **2.32:1 on white** and **1.17:1 on the deepest fill** -- below the package's own stated 3:1 non-text floor, below even the light theme's grey (`#9f9f9f`, 2.65:1), and effectively invisible on a dark fill, which is exactly what `test-print-palette.R:104` exists to prevent. Not defensible by any WCAG threshold. Palette 1 keeps its ink ladder untouched and takes **`#949494`** -- the lightest grey that still clears 3:1 (3.03:1 on white, 1.53:1 on the deepest fill, L\* 66.7 against rung 1's 45.0, so the reading order greyed < rung 1 < rung 2 stays plainly monotone). **Both existing WCAG assertions pass unchanged**, which is the check that chose the value. Palettes 2 and 3 declare `#888888`: their first rung is pure black, so they never needed a light grey. `tx_chrome_hex()` is a lookup now -- the chrome on paper is fixed (black on white, no hover) and the only thing a palette decides is how a cell is SET BACK -- and html, kableExtra, the plots, the aside and the ggplot legend guide follow for free, since all of them already funnelled through it.

**The marks: ONE cell suffix, two ladders.** `fmt_cell_suffix()` replaces the star block in `format()`: a palette's marks, or the significance stars, never both -- they sit in the same place after the value and say different things (how big, against the breaks; how sure, against a p-value). It needs **no direction logic of its own**: the mark is the SLOT's rendering exactly like the ink and the face, so the slot already carries the side and the magnitude, a greyed cell has slot 0 and takes none, and a footer row is excluded by the rule `get_stars()` already used. `format()` gains one formal, `theme = NULL` (= no palette, so tooltips and character casts stay annotation-free), passed by the four main display sites and by the composite expander for its PRIMARY token only.

**The glyphs are Unicode superscripts, and that is a measurement rather than a taste.** `⁺` / `⁻` are East-Asian **Neutral**, so every terminal draws them one cell wide and the character-count padding stays exact -- unlike the block glyphs of the row sparkline, which are Ambiguous and shift a CJK-configured terminal. That is recorded as a `WARNING` at the declaration. It also answers the two open questions in the brief. **Excel**: a data cell is a real NUMBER whose star rides the numFmt LITERAL, and a numFmt literal cannot carry a `vertAlign` run -- so a true Excel superscript would have meant demoting every marked column to text. Unicode codepoints go into that literal unchanged, and the cells stay numbers (`formatCode="0%⁺⁺"`). **Markdown** therefore needs no pandoc `^..^` and no change to `md_color_cell()`'s alignment maths at all -- the very thing the design doc's SS12.6 refused to drag in. **The width cost is not 4 characters**: the pad is to the column MAXIMUM, so a column whose strongest cell is rank 2 costs 2, exactly what `**` costs today, and only a column reaching rank 4 pays one character more than stars -- which it does not pay at all, since the marks REPLACE them.

**A doubled rule needed the face vocabulary widened, not a fourth flag.** `underline` went from a logical to `"" / "single" / "double"` -- OOXML's own words, so `create_font()` writes the value verbatim and `fmt_txt()` carries it into the Excel legend runs too. The five boundaries that only ask "is it ruled" take `nzchar()`; `tx_face_decls()` emits `text-decoration:underline double`; the transposed model flips it as a character (`slot_chr`, not `slot_lgl` -- which would have collapsed a doubled rule to TRUE and lost it); `font_id()`'s dedup key carries it, as every font aspect must. There is no markup for a doubled rule, so both ruled rungs emit `<u>` and the CSS class does the doubling -- the same trade the colour hexes already make against a class-stripping destination. Markdown loses nothing: its cells are pandoc spans carrying the slot class, so `tab_css()` doubles the rule there exactly as in html.

**On a graphics device a publication palette borrows its own grey ramp.** ggplot2's `fontface` has no underline and a plotted point has no face at all, so an all-black ink would collapse to one shade. `tx_plot_ink_family()` states the rule once: on a device the TEXT channel reads `bg_legend` -- the four-step dark ramp that already stands in for a fill wherever a fill is impossible -- keeping bold and italic beside it. `fmt_point_palette()`'s private `identical(theme, "print")` special case becomes a call to it, and `fmt_channel_codes()` gains an `ink` argument that only the `"plot"` backend sets. This RAISES palette 1's plot resolution (2 ink levels -> 4) and is what makes palettes 2 and 3 legible on a plot at all.

**The legend follows the palette, in three places.** A break-word now WEARS its slot's mark (`+10⁺⁺`), because under a marks palette nothing else tells the four thresholds apart -- and the mark joined `legend_break_tokens()`'s `look()` key, so the existing "drop a break that renders like the previous one" rule keeps collapsing palette 1's slots 3 and 4 and keeps all four of palette 2's. `tab_stars_legend()` returns NULL under a marks palette (no star is drawn, so none is explained). `legend_shade_names()` reads the palette's own `shade` pair -- closures, the `REG_WORDS$long` pattern, so `gettext()` runs at render and the msgids stay extractable -- and it is `NA` on a side the palette does not name typographically (palette 2's over side, both of palette 3's), where the legend then leads with the threshold instead of promising a distinction that is not there.

**And it stopped saying "Coloured" about a black-and-white table.** Under any publication palette the significance sentence now reads *"Marked: ... Unmarked: ..."*. One WHOLE sentence per variant, never a `%s` for the verb: a single word carries gender and number in French, which only a full-sentence msgid can get right. Three new msgids, translated (*"Marqué : ... Non marqué : ..."*); `po/R-tabxplor.pot` regenerated, `po/R-fr.po` merged and the `.mo` recompiled -- 243 translated, 10 fuzzy, 109 untranslated (all pre-existing debt for Phase 23f).

**Every palette now lives in one file.** `R/tab-print-palettes.R` became **`R/tab-palettes.R`** and took in the two literal blocks that were scattered elsewhere: the 24-bit OKLCH colour ramps and the 8-bit RStudio fallback (from `tab_classes.R`, moved VERBATIM -- their `oklch(...)` annotations are how the ramps were chosen and the only way to re-tune them), and `tx_chrome_hex()` (from `tab-css.R`). Five sections, general to specific: the colour ramps, the chrome, the publication grids, then the store and the ONE assembly that keys every palette by `(family, theme)`. `tab_classes.R` keeps the user-facing SURFACE (`set_color_palette()` / `get_color_style()` / the breaks) and `tab-css.R` the CSS vocabulary, each with a one-line pointer where the literals used to be -- so "what is this cell drawn with" is now one file rather than three, which is what the phase was about.

**`theme = "print_ready"` picks the palette from what the table IS.** A cross-table reads best with the MARKS -- nothing typographic then competes with the numbers, and a run of glyphs survives a plain-text copy -- while a regression reads best with the EMPHASIS ladder, because its cells already carry their own direction symbol (`+`/`-`, `x`/`div`), which frees the typography to spend everything on magnitude. The detection is a READ, not a guess: `tab_is_reg()` on `meta$spec$kind`, the declared table identity. It resolves in `resolve_export_opts(tabs =)` -- the one place a theme becomes concrete -- so every backend that styles itself is exact with no thought, and `tx_palette_theme()` applies the same fallback, so no palette lookup can be handed a key that does not exist. The old `"print"` is renamed **`print_minimalistic`** (which is what `"bw"` now means), giving four names: `print_ready` / `print_marks` / `print_emphasis` / `print_minimalistic`. ⚠ **The one caveat, and it is inherent**: the two arms write different `.p1..m4` rules while a stylesheet is table-INDEPENDENT by contract, so a document that emits `tab_css()` once and renders with `css = FALSE` carries only one of them. A cross-table is fine whatever it carries (its marks are cell text and need no rules at all); a regression's ladder is CSS and nothing else, so such a document names it -- which is exactly what `README.Rmd` now does. `print_rules` refuses both `print_ready` and `print_marks` for the same reason a media query cannot add characters to a page.

**A publication palette is a SHEET, and a sheet is all-or-nothing.** Measured on the shipped `README.md`: the tables carry ZERO inline colour (only `font-weight`), so on GitHub -- which strips `<style>`, `style=` and `class=` alike -- every table inherits the reader's own theme and is already correct in light and dark, with nothing of ours surviving to clash. That is what the `semantic` markup exists for. Where the stylesheet IS read (pkgdown, Quarto, a knitted page) there was a real mixing risk, and not a hypothetical one: the chrome was stated on the TABLE (0,1,0) and left the cells to inherit, but a host that colours the `<td>` directly beats an inherited value -- Bootstrap's `.table>:not(caption)>*>*` (0,1,1), which pkgdown stamps on every table -- so on a dark page the cells would have kept the page's dark ground inside a white table. The publication chrome is now stated again ON THE CELLS, at (0,1,1) deliberately: it ties the host and wins on source order (our stylesheet is emitted in the body, after its `<head>`), and still loses to our own `.tabxplor-tab .p1` (0,2,0), so an ink ladder is not flattened by it. The colour themes carry `""` there and are dropped -- light, dark and `auto` follow the page on purpose. ⚠ **Reported, not changed**: `.tabxplor-caption` is the one element left outside the sheet (it sits outside the `<table>`), so on a dark page a captioned table would show a black title on a dark ground. It is opt-in (`caption =`) and absent from the README; the two cures are to give it the sheet's background too (a full-width light strip above a content-width table) or to let it inherit the page like ordinary furniture -- a visual call rather than a technical one.

**One rule added late, and it cost less than a branch.** The cell suffix -- stars OR marks, in every theme, colour ones included -- now renders as a SUPPORTING piece: the chrome's `grey2`, with none of the cell's own bold / italic / underline, so the two annotations look alike everywhere and neither outshouts the number it qualifies. It needed no new code path, only one fact stated correctly: **the primary character range ends where the VALUE ends**, so the suffix falls outside it and `paint_split()` (console) and `html_cell_text()` (html) already draw it exactly as they draw an aside. Three recording sites moved -- a plain cell now gets a range it did not need before, the `mean (sigma sd)` branch records before pasting rather than after, and the composite expander subtracts the width its primary token wears (learned from the token's own `suffix_nchar`, not re-derived). Verified per medium: console wraps `1/2.68` in bold+red and then opens a separate grey style for the star; html emits `<i>1/1.29</i><span class="tx-sec">***</span>`. ⚠ **Markdown and Excel cannot honour the colour half**: md wraps a cell in ONE pandoc span and Excel folds the suffix into the numFmt literal, so in both the suffix takes the cell's colour -- the same whole-cell limitation their ASIDES already have, and fixing md would drag `md_color_cell()`'s width maths into per-piece widths. The face half holds everywhere.

**Four defects fixed on the way.** (1) **The cell suffix was landing in the ASIDE.** On a `mean (sigma sd)` cell the star was appended after the whole string, i.e. inside the `.tx-sec` piece, where it was drawn in the aside's grey and un-bolded -- against 22d-i's own "the face stops at the primary token" rule, and fatal for a mark, which IS the effect-size signal. The suffix is computed before the tail now, pasted onto the primary, and `primary_nchar` recorded around it -- measured, a `12.3*** (sigma2.0)` cell reports a primary span of `12.3***` where it used to report `12.3`. No golden moved: the fixtures carry no starred mean column, so the defect was reachable only in real use. (2) **`tab_xl()` starred a `contrib` column** that no other backend stars: it called `get_stars()` directly, skipping the `fmt_stars_applicable()` gate `format()` applies. Routing it through `fmt_cell_suffix()` deletes that private copy of the star logic and the divergence with it. (3) `roles$has_stars` -- which switches the number font to a monospace stack so the suffixes align -- counted stars only, so a marks table would have been rendered proportional; it counts the suffix now (the name stays: "stars" is what a reader calls the run of symbols after a number). (4) Two comments were describing code that had been hand-edited under them: `tx_chrome_hex()`'s *"3.54:1 on white, 1.79:1 on the darkest fill"* were `#888888`'s numbers, and the ink ladder's *"#333333, then #000000"* had become `#555555`. Plus one stranded `#' @keywords internal` attached to nothing, and the committed `golden.new.md`.

**Verified.** Targeted suite green while iterating (`print-palette` 125 passing, up from 88); the full suite at the end. The perceptual block of `test-print-palette.R` was NOT relaxed -- its two WCAG assertions are the ones that chose `#949494`, and they pass as written. Three tests added, all shaped so a fourth palette needs no fourth test: every declared grid is complete and ordered, its greys clear 3:1 and stay lighter than rung 1, its fill ramp IS the shared one, and marks and typography are never mixed; `print_emphasis` emits `underline double` in CSS and `<u val="double"/>` in the xlsx; `print_marks` marks in console / markdown / html / xlsx, drops the stars a colour palette keeps, and carries its marks into the legend. Twelve review files (a crosstab and a regression, html + xlsx, one pair per palette) are in `~/tabxplor_print_palettes` for the visual pass.

**Open, and named rather than pulled.** Palette 2's rungs 3 and 4 are one signal wherever there is no stylesheet (a Word paste, a plain-text markdown read, a plot): the legend collapses them there on its own, which is honest, but it IS a loss against html and Excel. And a console font lacking U+207A/U+207B will fall back to another face -- the console never selects a publication palette by default, so this only bites a user who sets `options(tabxplor.color_style_theme = "print_marks")` deliberately. **Nothing is owed to 22g**: neither jamovi module exposes `theme` at all (no hit in the four YAMLs), so the new palettes need no `jmvtools::prepare()`.
